articles.title: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview
articles.summary: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview. You can cache a DataFrame with df.cache() or df.persist() on serverless compute to reuse an expensive result for the rest of your session. Caching requires serverless environment version 5 or above, Databricks Connect for Python 18.1.8 or above, or Databricks Connect for Scala 18.1.5 or above. The preview is enabled by default for most workspaces. Workspace admins can disable it from the Previews page. See Cache DataFrames on serverless compute.

articles.title: Google Analytics Aggregated connector is available in Beta
articles.summary:
The managed Google Analytics Aggregated connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

Use the connector to ingest aggregated Google Analytics 4 report data, such as user activity, acquisition, engagement, monetization, demographics, and tech reports, into Databricks. You can also define custom reports with your own dimensions, metrics, and aggregation level. The connector supports incremental ingestion and both service account and OAuth user-to-machine (U2M) authentication.

articles.title: Files API 3.0 for Unity Catalog volumes is now in Beta
articles.summary:
Files API 3.0 is in Beta and introduces two new capabilities:

  • Multipart uploads: Upload files larger than 5 GB to Unity Catalog volumes.
  • Conditional operations: Upload, download, and delete files based on their current version to prevent unintended changes.

For more information, see What is Files API?.

articles.title: Box Audit Logs managed ingestion connector (Beta)
articles.summary: The Box Audit Logs connector in Lakeflow Connect is now available in Beta. Use the connector to ingest enterprise audit events from Box into Databricks. See Box Audit Logs connector.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Conversation outline: Use the conversation outline along the left edge of Genie One conversations to jump between your messages. Hover over a tick in the outline to preview a message and the start of its response. See Navigate a long conversation.
  • Upload skills (Public Preview): You can now click Upload skills to upload your existing skill files and folders to your skills folder in the workspace. See Upload a skill.
  • Snippets from external tool queries (Public Preview): Genie Ontology now also extracts snippets from queries that external tools, such as dbt, run on Databricks. These runs appear in query history alongside queries that you run in Databricks. See Genie Ontology.
  • Remembered sign-in email in the Genie mobile app (Public Preview): The Genie mobile app now remembers the email address of the last user who signed in and prefills it at the next sign-in. See Use Genie on mobile.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements
articles.summary:
• Private bookmarks: Dashboard viewers can now save filter combinations as private bookmarks to return to later. Private bookmarks are visible only to the user who creates them. See Save a private bookmark.
  • Bulk import from Power BI and Tableau: Genie Code can now import up to 100 Power BI or Tableau files at a time as AI/BI dashboards and metric views. See Import multiple files in bulk.
  • Field picker tooltips: Hovering over a field or measure name in the field picker now shows its full name in a tooltip.
  • Layered combo charts: Authors can now build combo charts from separate chart layers. See Combo chart.
  • Custom waterfall totals: Authors can now customize totals on waterfall charts. See Waterfall chart.
  • Sankey label improvements: Labels on Sankey diagrams now overlap less.

articles.title: Serverless job environments from pyproject.toml (Beta)
articles.summary: Serverless notebook and Python script tasks can use a pyproject.toml file to configure their job environment. Configure the project environment in the Jobs UI, the Jobs API, or a bundle. Workspace admins can enable Project-Scoped Shared Compute on the Previews page. See Configure a project environment with pyproject.toml.

articles.title: Shared Serverless for Asset Bundles (Beta)
articles.summary: With Shared Serverless for Asset Bundles, notebooks and files in the same bundle can share serverless compute and an environment defined in the bundle-root pyproject.toml file. Workspace admins can enable Project-Scoped Shared Compute on the Previews page. See Shared Serverless for Asset Bundles.

articles.title: Microsoft Entra ID connector is available in Beta
articles.summary:
The managed Microsoft Entra ID connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect.

Use the connector to ingest Microsoft Entra ID users, groups, applications, service principals, directory roles, identity configuration, and audit and sign-in logs into Databricks. The connector uses OAuth machine-to-machine authentication and supports incremental ingestion for audit and sign-in logs.

A Genie Code task runs your prompt autonomously as part of a job. It can read upstream task outputs and call tools as needed, and it returns a link to the resulting Genie Code chat with its response.

See Genie Code task for jobs.

articles.title: Lakebase Insights moves to per-project settings, with on-demand runs (Beta)
articles.summary:
Lakebase Insights now diagnoses issues using telemetry from the system.lakebase system tables and recommends next steps. The Lakebase Insights workspace preview enables automatic telemetry capture. Users with CAN MANAGE can configure Insights directly in each project's Settings, without creating an observability configuration.

This preview was previously named Lakebase Advanced Postgres Telemetry. Workspaces that used Insights before already have it enabled. To set up Insights:

  • If the preview isn't already enabled, ask a workspace admin to enable Lakebase Insights from the Previews page. Insights needs telemetry in system.lakebase to analyze a project, so enabling the Insights preview also enables Lakebase Observability in System Tables if it isn't already enabled. Workspace admins can enable the observability preview separately to capture telemetry without Insights.
  • To schedule Insights runs for a project, you need CAN MANAGE on that project. Enable Insights and set its analysis frequency in Settings.
  • You can run Insights on demand at any time, with or without a schedule.

If you scheduled Insights through an observability configuration, those jobs have stopped. Their schedules do not carry over. Those configurations no longer write telemetry to their Unity Catalog destinations, so their dashboards retain historical data but receive no new data.

To continue receiving scheduled insights, enable Insights and set an analysis frequency in each project's Settings. Each project runs separately, and each run uses compute and model tokens, so choose which projects to analyze and how often. Insights remains in Beta. See Detect issues with Insights.

articles.summary:

The boundary of the protected portion of the plan and its own metrics remain visible. Query results are unchanged. articles.title: Lakebase Search supports Chinese, Japanese, and Korean full-text search
articles.summary:
The lakebase_tokenizer extension now supports keyword search over Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK) text. These languages don't separate words with spaces, so native PostgreSQL full-text search can't split them into useful search terms. The new tokenizer_morph template uses morphological analysis with bundled language dictionaries to segment CJK text into words:

  • Built-in configurations: installing the extension creates tokenizer_chinese, tokenizer_japanese, and tokenizer_korean. Use them directly with to_tsvector without creating a dictionary.
  • Compound handling: choose a mode that keeps compound words whole, splits them into finer-grained terms, or emits both, depending on the language.
  • Language-aware filtering: drop Japanese particles and function words, convert Japanese terms to their base form, and filter Korean particles and endings, so matches focus on meaningful terms.

Like tokenizer_wholeword, it produces standard tsvector values that work with GIN (generalized inverted index) indexes and the lakebase_text lakebase_bm25 index for BM25 (best match 25) ranking. CJK support ships in lakebase_tokenizer 0.2.0. If you already use the extension, run ALTER EXTENSION lakebase_tokenizer UPDATE. Your existing configurations and indexes don't need to change. See lakebase_tokenizer.

articles.title: Replicate data in and out of Lakebase with Postgres logical replication
articles.summary: You can now use native Postgres logical replication to stream changes into and out of Lakebase. Migrate an existing Postgres database into Lakebase and keep it in sync until you cut over, or publish changes from Lakebase to external Postgres databases. See Logical replication.

articles.title: Consumer access to query Unity Gateway services is generally available
articles.summary:
Users with the consumer access entitlement no longer need an account admin to enable the "Consumer access to Unity Gateway" preview to query the model services and model provider services shared with them, or to use Unity Gateway coding agent features. See Consumer access capabilities.

This change can increase model traffic from consumer access users, including traffic to external providers. To control this traffic, account admins can set budgets and rate limits, or disable direct model access, for consumer access users. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway, Apply rate limits to model and MCP services, and Manage entitlements.

articles.title: Data Classification adds 50 new classes and support for 16 more countries and regions
articles.summary:
Data Classification now detects 50 new classes of sensitive data, along with new regional support for 16 countries and regions:

  • Payment card and financial data: Card security codes, card expiration dates, card track data, card PINs, SWIFT codes, and credit scores.
  • Personal and employee data: Gender, residency status, disability data, sexual data, street addresses, geographic coordinates, compensation, and employment status.
  • Software security secrets: Credentials and secrets used by software.
  • Regional identifiers: Added 35 new classes and expanded coverage in existing classes across 18 countries and regions, including China, Mexico, the UK, other European countries, and more. See the documentation for details.

Regional tags are available in select regions. See Supported classification tags.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Flash (Beta): Agent mode now offers Flash, an option that prioritizes response speed over depth. Flash is most efficient on simpler, everyday tasks. See Flash.
  • Agent mode model upgrade: Agent mode now uses upgraded models that better handle long context and respond faster. See Agent mode.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Collaborative document editing: People you share a Genie One document with can now edit it if they have CAN EDIT permission. See Share a document.
  • Group memberships in user info: When Genie One retrieves a user's information, it now also returns the user's group memberships. You can use workspace instructions and table descriptions to tailor how Genie One responds to members of specific groups.
  • Reuse context from past investigations: When you ask a question similar to one you asked before, Genie One can now use the context from the earlier investigation to answer faster. See Recall past conversations.
  • Share skills with Unity Gateway (Beta): You can now publish Genie One skills to a Unity Catalog schema and share them with your team. Unity Gateway governs shared skills, so teammates can discover and install existing skills from one central location instead of keeping copies in sync. See Share a skill with your team.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Lakehouse Real-Time warehouse support (Beta): AI/BI dashboards now work with Lakehouse Real-Time SQL warehouses. See Use Lakehouse Real-Time with AI/BI dashboards.
  • Dashboard Insights (Beta): Viewers can now have Genie analyze the charts on a published dashboard page and summarize notable findings, such as trends and outliers, as insight cards. See Dashboard Insights.
  • Import Power BI .tmdl files: Authors can now upload Power BI .tmdl files to create metric views with the /importBI Genie Code skill. See Import one file at a time.
  • Pivot table drill-down: Viewers can now drill down through the row and column hierarchy of a pivot table one level at a time. See Drill down in pivot tables.
  • Theme fonts for rich text titles: Rich text widget titles and descriptions now inherit the dashboard theme's font styles. See Customize colors and fonts.
  • Pivot table null header fix: Pivot tables now show NULL values and the text null as separate headers instead of merging them into one.
  • Cross-dataset measure export fix: Exported cross-dataset measures now use the measure name as the column header.
  • Decimal precision fix: Visualizations that Genie generates now respect decimal precision.

articles.title: ADBC driver for Power BI is now generally available
articles.summary: The Arrow Database Connectivity (ADBC) driver for the Databricks connector for Power BI is now generally available. ADBC is the default driver for new connections in Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service. See Configure ADBC or ODBC driver for Power BI.

articles.title: MySQL integrated CDC pipeline is now generally available
articles.summary: The integrated CDC pipeline for MySQL is now generally available. An integrated CDC pipeline ingests change data from MySQL into Databricks using a single pipeline, combining extraction and application into one pipeline update. Unlike the standard gateway-based architecture, an integrated CDC pipeline requires no separate ingestion gateway. See Create an integrated CDC pipeline for MySQL.

articles.title: Data Classification adds 50 new classes and support for 16 more countries and regions
articles.summary:
Data Classification now detects 50 new classes of sensitive data, along with new regional support for 16 countries and regions:

  • Payment card and financial data: Card security codes, card expiration dates, card track data, card PINs, SWIFT codes, and credit scores.
  • Personal and employee data: Gender, residency status, disability data, sexual data, street addresses, geographic coordinates, compensation, and employment status.
  • Software security secrets: Credentials and secrets used by software.
  • Regional identifiers: Added 35 new classes and expanded coverage in existing classes across 18 countries and regions, including China, Mexico, the UK, other European countries, and more. See the documentation for details.

articles.summary:

This change can increase model traffic from consumer access users, including traffic to external providers. To control this traffic, account admins can set budgets and rate limits, or disable direct model access, for consumer access users. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway, Apply rate limits to model and MCP services, and Manage entitlements.

articles.title: Redesigned MLflow Logs tab for AI Runtime runs
articles.summary: The MLflow run page Logs tab for AI Runtime runs now supports searching and filtering logs by node, level, and time range, following a running workload as new output arrives, and downloading logs. For new runs, it replaces the log files previously stored on the run's Artifacts tab, which are deprecated. Logs are available for 60 days. Logs for existing runs remain on the Artifacts tab. See View logs in the MLflow Logs tab.

articles.title: The agentic code converter is generally available for SQL conversion
articles.summary:
The agentic code converter is now generally available for the SQL target framework. Powered by Genie Code, it converts SQL from dialects such as T-SQL, Snowflake, Redshift, Oracle, BigQuery, and Teradata into Databricks SQL queries. You organize the work in a migration project, and the converter validates the output and fixes errors before writing the results to a workspace folder. After a conversion, you can continue chatting with Genie Code about the converted files to address action items or summarize the changes.

See Convert SQL with the agentic code converter.

articles.title: Workspace-level package repositories for Databricks Apps will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Starting November 13, 2026, workspace-level package repositories for Databricks Apps will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Workspace admins can configure default Python and npm package repositories that apps inherit while still allowing app-level overrides.

See Configure default package repositories.

articles.title: Data Classification API is now generally available
articles.summary: The Data Classification API and its Terraform resource are now generally available. Auto-tagging configuration (auto_tag_configs) remains in Public Preview. See the API reference.

articles.title: Transactions support both managed Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg tables
articles.summary:
Transactions are generally available for both Unity Catalog managed Delta Lake tables and Unity Catalog managed Apache Iceberg tables. Group multiple SQL statements across one or more managed Delta Lake or managed Apache Iceberg tables into a single atomic transaction using BEGIN ATOMIC ... END; or BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... COMMIT; syntax. Transactions require catalog commits enabled on participating tables.

See Transactions.

articles.title: Data Classification API is now generally available
articles.summary: The Data Classification API and its Terraform resource are now generally available. Auto-tagging configuration (auto_tag_configs) remains in Public Preview. See the API reference.

articles.title: Workspace-level package repositories for Databricks Apps are generally available
articles.summary:
Workspace admins can now configure default Python and npm package repositories for Databricks Apps. Apps inherit the workspace configuration while still allowing app-level overrides.

See Configure default package repositories.

articles.title: AI Runtime will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled

AI Runtime is scheduled to become generally available on October 15, 2026, on AWS and Azure for workspaces without the compliance security profile enabled.

AI Runtime will be available by default for eligible workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in mid November. Availability depends on the supported compliance standards and regions.

Use AI Runtime to train and fine-tune models on serverless GPUs without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure.

See AI Runtime.

articles.summary:
Google Gemini 4 Argon is now available on Unity Gateway. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: On-demand state repartitioning is now generally available
articles.summary: On-demand state repartitioning is now generally available. You can resize the number of shuffle partitions for a stateful Structured Streaming query or Lakeflow pipeline without losing checkpoint state. See On-demand state repartitioning for stateful streaming queries.

articles.title: Google Gemini 4 Argon is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
Google Gemini 4 Argon is now available on Unity Gateway. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

articles.summary: External engines can now query Unity Catalog views over Delta Lake tables through the Unity REST API. See External access to views.

articles.title: Cribl connector is available in Beta
articles.summary:
The managed Cribl connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect.

Use the connector to ingest Cribl.Cloud Worker Group configuration, worker and health status, organization metadata, and Leader audit and access logs into Databricks. The connector uses OAuth machine-to-machine authentication and supports incremental ingestion for audit and access logs.

articles.title: Shared output in clean rooms is now generally available
articles.summary: Clean room runs can now write to a shared output schema that every collaborator can read as soon as each table is created, even before the run finishes. Use it to share results, logs, and debugging information with all collaborators. See Share output with all collaborators.

articles.title: JAR workloads in clean rooms are now generally available
articles.summary: You can now run compiled Java or Scala code in clean rooms. Run a JAR as its own clean room analysis, or register a function from a JAR and call it from a clean room notebook as a temporary UDF. See Run JAR workloads in Databricks clean rooms.

articles.title: Create clean rooms with identity resolution providers in one step (GA)
articles.summary: You can now create a ready-to-use packaged clean room with an approved identity resolution provider, such as Acxiom, Adstra, LiveRamp, or The Trade Desk, in one step from the Clean Rooms page. The provider is preconfigured as the package provider, so you can add your data and run the provider's analysis right away. See Create a clean room with an identity resolution provider.

articles.title: Databricks AI Runtime SDK replaces serverless_gpu
articles.summary:
Starting in GPU environment version 6, the Databricks AI Runtime SDK (databricks-sdk-air) replaces the deprecated serverless_gpu package. It provides the @distributed and ray_init APIs and the databricks.air.data utilities under the databricks.air namespace. The gpus and gpu_type arguments are renamed to num_accelerators and accelerator_type. The old names still work in databricks.air but emit a FutureWarning, and support will end in version 7.

Serverless GPU environment version 6 includes both packages. Version 6 is the last version that includes serverless_gpu. Versions 5 and below continue to use it. See Migrate from serverless_gpu.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.42 is now available in Preview
articles.summary:
Databricks SQL version 2026.42 is now available in the Preview channel. This version includes the following changes:

  • Operating system security updates.
  • Miscellaneous bug fixes.

This version doesn't include new features or behavioral changes.

articles.title: Feature Views will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Feature Views are now generally available. They will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in mid-November 2026.

Define and compute features declaratively from batch or streaming data, then use them for model training and online serving.

See Feature Views.

articles.title: Unity Gateway Skills API and developer tools are available in Beta
articles.summary:
The Unity Gateway Skills REST API is now available in Beta, with create, read, update, list, delete, and finalize support across Databricks developer tools:

  • Databricks CLI
  • Python SDK
  • Go SDK
  • Go Modular SDK
  • Java SDK
  • JavaScript SDK

See the Skills API and SDK reference.

articles.title: Governed tag propagation is in Beta
articles.summary:
Tag propagation in Unity Catalog is in Beta. When you enable tag propagation for a governed tag, Unity Catalog uses lineage to automatically apply that tag to derived tables and views whenever a supported operation runs, such as CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, CREATE VIEW, INSERT INTO ... SELECT, or MERGE. This keeps classification and ABAC enforcement consistent at both the table and column levels as data moves downstream.

See Tag propagation.

articles.title: Parameters for Lakeflow pipelines are now generally available
articles.summary: Pipeline parameters are now generally available. Parameterize Lakeflow pipeline SQL source code with key-value pairs so a single pipeline can run against different catalogs, schemas, or tables without editing the source. Define parameter defaults in pipeline settings, override them when you start an update, and reference them in SQL with named parameter syntax. See Use parameters with pipelines.

articles.title: Private connectivity from serverless compute to AWS-managed resources is now generally available
articles.summary: AWS Private Link from Databricks serverless compute to AWS-managed resources, such as S3 buckets, previously in Public Preview, is now generally available. Your data traffic remains entirely within the AWS network and never traverses the public internet. See Configure private connectivity to AWS-managed resources.

articles.title: Agent memory pipelines are in Beta
articles.summary: Agent memory pipelines are in Beta. A memory pipeline connects a session store to a memory store. Each run uses an LLM to distill durable facts, preferences, and decisions from stored conversations into memory entries that your agent recalls in later conversations. You can run a pipeline on demand or about every 24 hours. See Agent memory pipelines.

articles.title: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are now legacy
articles.summary: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are now legacy offerings. For new agents written in code, Databricks recommends the Agent Bricks CLI. To build agents without code, use Genie Agents. See Legacy agent offerings.

articles.title: Feature Views are now generally available
articles.summary: Feature Views are now generally available for batch, streaming, and request-time data. They will be enabled for compliance security profile workspaces in mid-November 2026. See Feature Views.

articles.title: Context-based ingress policies for inbound private connectivity are now generally available
articles.summary: Context-based ingress policies for inbound Private Link are now generally available. Control which registered VPC endpoints can reach your workspaces, and combine endpoint rules with identity and request type conditions in the same policy. If Context-Based Ingress: Workspace Private Access Policies isn't already enabled for your account, an account admin can enable it from the account console Previews page. See Configure private access policy.

articles.title: JDBC Unity Catalog connections will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
In mid-November 2026, JDBC Unity Catalog connections, including support for SSL certificates, will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

Use JDBC Unity Catalog connections to connect to external databases with a custom JDBC driver, with access governed by Unity Catalog.

See JDBC connection.

articles.title: Use OpenJev as the evaluator for LLM-as-a-judge service policies (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now select OpenJev (Qwen3.5 4B) as the evaluator model service of a custom LLM-as-a-judge service policy. OpenJev classifies content without generating output tokens, so it typically responds faster than a chat evaluator. See Use OpenJev as the evaluator.

articles.title: Use request tags in Unity Gateway service policies (Beta)
articles.summary: Custom service policies in Unity Gateway can now check caller-supplied request tags, such as requiring a tag before a model request or MCP tool call proceeds. See Request tags.

articles.title: Unity Gateway supports Amazon Bedrock Mantle
articles.summary: You can now access Amazon Bedrock Mantle models through Unity Gateway model provider services, with Unity Catalog permissions, rate limits, budgets, and inference tables. See Model providers external to Databricks.

articles.title: Code execution in Genie One (Public Preview)
articles.summary: Genie One can now run code in a secure, isolated sandbox to take on work that goes beyond SQL, such as more advanced analyses. Code runs on your behalf using your existing permissions, so Unity Catalog governance and data access controls continue to apply. See Code execution in Genie One.

articles.title: Use request tags in Unity Gateway service policies (Beta)
articles.summary: Custom service policies in Unity Gateway can now check caller-supplied request tags, such as requiring a tag before a model request or MCP tool call proceeds. See Request tags.

articles.title: Use OpenJev as the evaluator for LLM-as-a-judge service policies (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now select OpenJev (Qwen3.5 4B) as the evaluator model service of a custom LLM-as-a-judge service policy. OpenJev classifies content without generating output tokens, so it typically responds faster than a chat evaluator. See Use OpenJev as the evaluator.

articles.title: Google Workspace connector is available in Beta
articles.summary:
The managed Google Workspace connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect.

Use the connector to ingest audit activity from Google Workspace applications and services into Databricks. The connector uses OAuth user authorization and supports incremental ingestion.

articles.title: Unity Gateway supports Amazon Bedrock Mantle
articles.summary: You can now access Amazon Bedrock Mantle models through Unity Gateway model provider services, with Unity Catalog permissions, rate limits, budgets, and inference tables. See Model providers external to Databricks.

articles.title: Unity Catalog Scala and Java UDFs and Scalar and Batch Unity Catalog Python UDFs will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Unity Catalog Scala and Java UDFs and Scalar and Batch Unity Catalog Python UDFs will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in November 2026.

See Python UDF feature requirements and Scala and Java user-defined functions (UDFs) in Unity Catalog.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Connect to external tools (Beta): A Genie Agent can now search and take actions in external tools like Google Drive and Microsoft 365 through MCP connectors. See Connect a Genie Agent to external tools and sources.
  • Automatic content search on attached volumes (Beta): When you attach a volume to a Genie Agent, Databricks now automatically enables content search for it. See How content search works.
  • Automatic volume sync (Beta): Content search now stays in sync with attached volumes automatically. When you add, change, or remove files, Databricks updates the index without any manual step. See How content search works.
  • Volumes from restricted catalogs (Beta): You can now attach a volume as a source for a Genie Agent even when the volume's catalog isn't accessible from the agent's workspace by default, such as a catalog that is bound to specific workspaces. See Attach volumes to a Genie Agent.
  • File upload fix: Fixed a bug where uploading a file to a Genie Agent through Genie One created duplicate conversations.
  • Deletion warning for sources and instructions: Deleting sources or instructions from a Genie Agent now asks you to confirm to prevent accidental deletions.
  • Column display name fix: Fixed a bug where Genie Code did not update column display names in a Genie Agent.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Faceted counters: You can now facet a counter visualization to show one counter tile per dimension value. See Faceting.
  • Legend cross-filtering: Selecting an item in a visualization's legend now applies cross-filtering. See Apply cross-filtering.
  • Dashboard task page selection and tabular attachments: Dashboard tasks in jobs can now optionally include dashboard page selection and tabular attachments. See Configure a dashboard task.
  • Date filter month picker fix: Fixed a bug where the month drop-down menu on date filters did not respect your dark or light mode preference.

articles.title: Productboard connector is available in Beta
articles.summary:
The managed Productboard connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

Use the connector to ingest product hierarchy, roadmap, objectives, customer feedback notes, and workspace member data from Productboard into Databricks. The connector uses Server-to-Server OAuth authentication and supports incremental ingestion for notes, UI-based pipeline authoring, Declarative Automation Bundles, and API-based pipeline authoring.

articles.title: The Discover page and domains are now GA
articles.summary: The Discover page and domains are now generally available. Discover is a curated browsing experience that helps users find assets across Databricks without requiring deep knowledge of catalog hierarchies. Use domains and subdomains to organize assets such as tables, dashboards, notebooks, and Genie Agents by business area, highlight key assets with custom curation, and explore AI-recommended assets.

articles.title: Azure DevOps connector is available in Beta
articles.summary:
The managed Azure DevOps connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect.

Use the connector to ingest project, repository, work item, build, release, and identity data from Azure DevOps into Databricks. The connector authenticates with a Microsoft Entra service principal and supports incremental ingestion of commits.

articles.title: Enforce partner guardrails with external service policies (Beta)

An external service policy sends request and response content to your guardrail vendor and blocks the call when the vendor denies it, with no changes to your applications. See Enforce a partner guardrail with an external service policy.

articles.title: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW will soon preserve grants, comments and tags by default
articles.summary:
Starting December 2, 2026, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW will update views in-place, instead of dropping and re-creating the view. Grants, tags, and comments are preserved with one caveat:

  • You must first remove governed tags on a view column before dropping the column via CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW. Otherwise, the statement will fail with a CANNOT_DROP_TAGGED_COLUMN error to protect the ABAC policies that depend on them (learn more).

Use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW <catalog>.<schema>.<view> NOCOPY * … to drop grants, tags and comments on view explicitly (governed tags are still retained).

See CREATE VIEW and Upcoming change to CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW metadata preservation.

articles.title: Metric view window measures are generally available
articles.summary: Window measures in metric views are now generally available. Window measures define rolling window, cumulative, or semiadditive aggregations, such as moving averages, period-over-period changes, and running totals. See Window measures.

articles.title: Agent Bricks documentation for code-first agent development
articles.summary:
The Agent Bricks documentation now centers on building, deploying, and running custom agents in code. See Develop agents on Databricks:

  • Agent compute stack: New pages describe how a deployed agent's framework or harness, agent server, and agent runtime fit together. See Deploy agents on Databricks.
  • DurableAgentServer and Agent Runtime: DurableAgentServer serves agents through the invocation API, with synchronous, streaming, and background runs, persistent run state, and crash recovery. Agent Runtime runs it on Databricks Apps. See Agent Server and Agent Runtime.
  • Querying agents: The query guide is organized by agent server, starting with the invocation API. See Query agents deployed on Databricks.
  • Legacy offerings: Offerings that are no longer recommended for new agents, including the MLflow AgentServer, LongRunningAgentServer, and agents deployed to Model Serving, are now in a Legacy section that maps each one to its replacement. See Legacy agent offerings.

• Materialize SQL datasets (Beta): Dashboard materialization now covers SQL datasets in addition to local metric views, so you can materialize a dashboard's SQL datasets. See Dataset materialization in AI/BI dashboards.

  • Genie Code for dashboard authoring: New authoring capabilities and fixes for Genie Code:
    • Genie Code can now use images stored in your workspace as image widgets, not only uploaded files.

articles.title: Lakebase Search adds a configurable text tokenizer for keyword search
articles.summary:
The new lakebase_tokenizer extension lets you control how Lakebase Search turns text into search terms, so keyword search matches the way your data and users actually read. Native PostgreSQL full-text search gives you little control over this step. lakebase_tokenizer adds a configurable whole-word tokenizer through PostgreSQL's standard text-search dictionary interface, with the controls that matter for relevance:

  • Normalization: lowercase text, apply Unicode normalization for byte-stable matching, and strip accents so café matches cafe.
  • Stopwords and synonyms: manage your own stopword and synonym lists in SQL, so terms like usa and united_states match the same rows.
  • Stemming and possessives: reduce words to their root with a native English stemmer and strip trailing 's, so running matches run and John's matches john.

It produces standard tsvector values, so a tokenizer you configure works with to_tsvector, GIN (generalized inverted index) indexes, and the lakebase_text lakebase_bm25 index for BM25 (best match 25) ranking. Install it after enabling Lakebase Search in your project settings. See lakebase_tokenizer.

articles.title: Deleting a Unity Catalog pipeline now retains tables by default
articles.summary:
When you delete a Unity Catalog pipeline that uses the default publishing mode, the UI and the Pipelines DELETE API retain associated materialized views, streaming tables, and views by default. The retained tables can be queried but cannot be updated until moved into an active pipeline. To delete a pipeline and its tables together, set the cascade field to true in the API request. This change does not affect Hive metastore pipelines.

See Delete a pipeline and Delete a pipeline.

articles.title: The Genie One MCP server is now generally available
articles.summary:
The Genie One MCP server is now generally available as a Databricks-provided MCP Service, system.ai.genie_one_mcp, in Unity Gateway. It exposes Genie as a conversational tool over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so any MCP client or agent, such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor, can ground its data questions in Genie's trusted insights, with Unity Catalog permissions enforced on every request. See Genie One MCP server.

The previous Beta endpoint, https://<workspace-hostname>/api/2.0/mcp/genie, is deprecated and will be sunset on October 31, 2026. Move all workloads to the system.ai.genie_one_mcp MCP Service before then.

articles.title: Genie Code can now build intelligent document processing pipelines
articles.summary: Genie Code can now build end-to-end document processing pipelines by orchestrating parsing, classification, extraction, and validation. Point it at unstructured PDFs, contracts, or invoices, and it evaluates extraction quality against labeled data and iterates to improve it. See Use Genie Code for intelligent document processing.

articles.title: Sharing metric views with OpenSharing is now generally available
articles.summary: Sharing metric views with OpenSharing is now generally available. Add metric views to a share and query them with MEASURE(...) on serverless compute. See Add metric views to a share and Read shared metric views.

articles.title: Lakeflow Designer September Release
articles.summary:
The Lakeflow Designer September release adds Guardrails, multi-input joins, new parameter controls, and more ways to bring data into a visual data prep. The following updates are now available:

  • Create a visual data prep from multiple files: On the Visual data prep page, select Import file > As source to upload multiple files into one visual data prep, with a Source operator for each file. See Start a visual data prep from files.
  • Guardrails operator: Check data against rules such as not null, unique, and accepted values. Choose whether failed checks warn, block passing rows, or stop the workflow. See Guardrails.
  • Default preview row limit: Set the preview row limit for all operators from the Preview menu in the toolbar. Override it for individual operators when needed. See Control how much data previews process.
  • Join three or more inputs: Use one Join operator for three or more tables, with a relationship for each additional input. See Join.
  • More Pivot aggregation choices: The Pivot operator now offers functions based on the value column's data type, including FIRST, LAST, and CONCAT where supported. See Pivot.
  • Parameterize Combine and Limit operators: Use parameters in Combine and Limit settings, or to enable and disable operators at run time. See Use parameters in Lakeflow Designer.
  • Create a user-defined operator with Genie Code: From the Operators menu, describe a transformation and review the generated configuration and Python function before adding the operator to your visual data prep. See Create a local user-defined operator with Genie Code.
  • Continue from an Output operator: Connect downstream operators to an Output operator to continue working with the data after it writes to a destination. See Output.
  • Advanced CSV and Excel file output: Split output by distinct values into files or Excel worksheets, set a worksheet name or cell range, and choose whether to include headers. See Output.
  • Detect code changes made outside the editor: Designer detects operator code changed through Git or a bundle deployment and prevents editor and Genie Code edits until you regenerate the code from its configuration. See Handle externally modified operator code.
  • Drag a workspace file onto the canvas: Drag a file from the workspace file browser onto the canvas to add it as a Source operator.
  • Sort operators in the Table of Contents: Expand groups to find their operators, and sort the list by graph order, name, type, or status. See Sort and filter the list.
  • Create an external database connection from Source: Create a Unity Catalog connection and foreign catalog from an unconfigured Source operator, then select a table from the catalog.

articles.title: ai_search can search Lakebase synced tables (Beta)
articles.summary:
The ai_search function can now retrieve from Lakebase synced tables with Lakebase Search enabled, in addition to AI Search indexes. Add a lakebase_search knowledge source to search a Lakebase synced table, or combine it with vector_search sources in the same call. This feature is in Beta.

See ai_search function.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Monitoring table column picker: You can now choose which columns appear in the agent monitoring table on the Monitor tab. See Monitor the agent.
  • Page-level citations for volume files (Beta): When a Genie Agent answers using content retrieved from an attached volume, its citations can now point to the specific page of the source file. See How a Genie Agent analyzes files.

articles.title: Service principal Genie usage is billed at standard pricing
articles.summary: Genie usage by service principals is now billed at standard Genie pay-as-you-go pricing. Service principals are excluded from the free monthly usage allowance that applies to individual users. See Manage budgets and cost controls for Genie and Monitor and understand your Genie cost.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Pin a chat: You can now pin a chat to keep it at the top of the sidebar. See Manage chats in the sidebar.
  • Larger file uploads: You can now upload files larger than 10 MB to a Genie One conversation. See Upload a file.
  • Automatic tool action approval: Genie One can now automatically approve tool actions for the rest of a chat. An AI classifier checks each action against your request and blocks any that fall outside its scope.
  • MCP writes in the mobile app (Beta): The Genie One mobile app now supports MCP write actions from connected tools. See Connect Genie One to external tools and sources.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Data-exploration controls in dataset results and metric view preview: The dataset results table and the metric view preview grid now include column pinning and formatting, search, a column explorer, natural-language filtering, and a selection details panel. See View the results table.
  • Include-style level of detail (LOD) expressions in the metric view editor: The metric view editor now supports include-style LOD expressions. See Finer level of detail.
  • Ignore filters on a widget: You can now configure a dashboard widget to ignore selected dashboard filters, so those filters don't affect the widget while they continue to apply to the rest of the page. See Ignore filters for a widget.
  • Genie Code stall fix: Fixed an issue where Genie Code made unnecessary turns between edits, which made the agent appear to stall.
  • Field labels error fix: Fixed an issue where selecting a field for labels caused a dashboard error.
  • Data reference picker fix: Fixed an issue where the @ data reference picker displayed a transparent background.

articles.title: Lakebase observability telemetry in system tables (Beta)
articles.summary: Lakebase captures its Postgres observability telemetry into the system.lakebase system tables, with no configuration to create and no destination to choose. Query plans, session history, wait events, schema-change history, database and compute health, and Postgres logs land there, and records are retained for 7 days. Account admins and metastore admins can read the tables and manage access to them, and a user with access queries the telemetry the way they would any Unity Catalog table. See Lakebase telemetry in system tables.

articles.title: Scalar and Batch Unity Catalog Python UDFs are now generally available
articles.summary:
Scalar and Batch Unity Catalog Python UDFs are now generally available on all supported compute types. This release adds named handlers for row-at-a-time scalar UDFs, removes the five-UDF-call-per-query limit, and aligns scalar TIMESTAMP inputs with PySpark behavior. You can also install custom dependencies and access Unity Catalog service credentials and secrets from your functions. Some capabilities require the UDF definition to explicitly set environment_version to 6 or above, including the newly generally available scalar capabilities on serverless compute. Requirements vary by feature and compute type. See Python UDF feature requirements.

For workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled, see What's coming for planned availability changes.

articles.title: Scala UDFs can access Unity Catalog secrets
articles.summary: Session-scoped and Unity Catalog Scala UDFs can now access secrets managed in Unity Catalog. Session-scoped UDFs use the caller's permissions. A Unity Catalog Scala UDF declares secrets in its SECRETS clause and uses the function owner's permissions, so callers do not need direct access to the secrets. On serverless compute, secret access from session-scoped Scala UDFs requires environment version 6 or above. A Unity Catalog Scala UDF that accesses a secret must set environment_version to 6 or above. On classic compute, secret access requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above with standard access mode. Among SQL warehouse types, only serverless SQL warehouses support Unity Catalog Scala UDFs that access secrets. Direct invocation is not supported on dedicated access mode compute. See Secrets in Unity Catalog.

articles.title: Build governed data and AI apps without code (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now build governed data and AI apps without code. Genie App Builder builds apps from natural-language prompts inside an App Space that enforces governance, and the apps scale to zero when idle. See Genie App Builder.

articles.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro (0813) is scheduled for retirement
articles.summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro (0813) will be retired on October 30, 2026. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the recommended replacement. See Deprecated and retired models for migration guidance.

articles.title: Time travel queries now enforce ABAC policies (Beta)
articles.summary: This feature is in Beta. Starting in Databricks Runtime 19, you can use time travel on qualifying Unity Catalog managed tables while enforcing ABAC row filter and column mask policies. See Time travel with ABAC policies.

articles.title: Variant shredding will soon be enabled by default on new Variant tables
articles.summary:
Starting November 18, 2026, Databricks will automatically add the variantShredding table feature to new tables that contain a column of the VARIANT type when they are created on Databricks Runtime 17.3 or above. Variant shredding stores frequently accessed fields in a typed, columnar layout to improve query performance.

This is a breaking change for Databricks Runtime 15.4: clusters running Databricks Runtime 15.4 can't read from or write to tables that have variant shredding enabled. Upgrade affected clusters to Databricks Runtime 16.4 or above before this change takes effect.

See Use variant shredding to optimize performance.

articles.title: Bundled BigQuery JDBC driver removal in Databricks Runtime 20
articles.summary:
Starting with Databricks Runtime 20, Databricks Runtime no longer includes the bundled BigQuery JDBC driver, while Databricks Runtime 19 and earlier continue to include it.

Classic compute workloads that use Spark JDBC with a jdbc:bigquery: URL fail with a driver-not-found error unless a BigQuery JDBC driver is installed. Before upgrading an affected workload, migrate the workload.

articles.title: Lakebase backup schedule API (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now manage Lakebase backup schedules programmatically. The backup schedule API lets you read and set a root branch's automated snapshot cadences (daily, weekly, or monthly) and how long each cadence's snapshots are retained. This API is in Beta and available to all Lakebase workspaces. See Create a backup schedule.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.38 is now available in Preview
articles.summary:
Databricks SQL version 2026.38 is now available in the Preview channel. Review the following section to learn about new features and behavioral changes.

Truncate numbers without rounding using truncate

The truncate function truncates a number to a specified scale without rounding.

Remove array elements with trim_array

The trim_array function removes the specified number of elements from the end of an array, or from the beginning when the count is negative.

current_oauth_custom_identity_claim returns NULL when no claim is present

The current_oauth_custom_identity_claim function now returns NULL instead of raising OAUTH_CUSTOM_IDENTITY_CLAIM_NOT_PROVIDED when the session has no custom identity claim. A row filter that combines the claim with another predicate using OR can now evaluate its other conditions. Because the claim is NULL when absent, a comparison against it doesn't match. This change is rolling out gradually.

articles.title: Databricks Runtime 19: September 21, 2026
articles.summary:
New features and improvements

  • truncate function: SQL and the Scala and Python DataFrame APIs now support truncate, which truncates a number to a specified scale without rounding.
  • trim_array function: SQL and the Scala and Python DataFrame APIs now support trim_array, which removes elements from the end of an array when the count is positive or from the beginning when the count is negative.
  • Session environment variables for Python user-defined function workers: Set a session-scoped Python worker environment variable using the spark.pythonWorkerEnv.<variable-name> configuration prefix. The variables apply when workers for regular scalar Python user-defined functions (UDFs) are launched.
  • Auto-optimized shuffle v2 enabled by default: Auto-optimized shuffle v2 is now used when you do not set a fixed number of shuffle partitions. Workloads that explicitly set a fixed shuffle partition count are unchanged.

Behavioral changes

  • current_oauth_custom_identity_claim() returns NULL when no identity claim is present: current_oauth_custom_identity_claim() now returns NULL instead of raising OAUTH_CUSTOM_IDENTITY_CLAIM_NOT_PROVIDED (SQLSTATE 22KD2) when the session has no custom identity claim, so a row filter that ORs the claim with another predicate can still evaluate its other branches. A comparison against the claim never matches when the claim is absent. This change is rolling out gradually.

articles.title: Configure provider discounts for external model spend
articles.summary:
Unity Gateway estimates external model spend using each provider's published list prices. If your organization has negotiated different pricing with a provider, you can now configure a price multiplier on the model provider service so that spend estimates reflect those rates.

Price multipliers only apply to external models accessed through model provider services, not Databricks-hosted partner models.

See Configure a price multiplier.

articles.title: Lakebase Search is generally available
articles.summary:
Lakebase Search is now generally available. It brings scalable vector and keyword search to Lakebase projects through two Postgres extensions, so you can run semantic and exact-term search in a single database without a separate search stack:

  • lakebase_vector adds the lakebase_ann index type for approximate nearest-neighbor vector search. It is drop-in compatible with pgvector, using the same types, operators, and query syntax, and scales to over 1 billion vectors on a single index with builds up to 50-100x faster than HNSW.
  • lakebase_text adds the lakebase_bm25 index type for BM25 full-text search. It works with standard tsvector types and operators, adding BM25 ranking and top-K pushdown that PostgreSQL's native GIN index does not provide.

Indexes are storage-backed, so they are available immediately after scale-to-zero without warmup. Combine both extensions for hybrid search that returns semantic and exact-term matches in one ranked list. To get started, enable Lakebase Search in your project settings, then install the extensions.

See Lakebase Search, lakebase_vector, and lakebase_text.

articles.title: Databricks Apps telemetry is now generally available
articles.summary:
Configuring telemetry for your Databricks apps is now generally available. Databricks Apps telemetry collects traces, logs, and metrics and persists them to Unity Catalog tables using the OpenTelemetry (OTel) protocol. After you enable app telemetry, Databricks automatically captures system logs and usage events, and you can add custom instrumentation using the OpenTelemetry SDK for your framework.

See Configure telemetry for Databricks Apps.

articles.title: Databricks Apps is now on by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Databricks Apps is now on by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

articles.summary:
Unity Gateway now supports all compliance security profile standards supported by Databricks and is available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

articles.title: Metastore-level ABAC policies are in Beta
articles.summary:
Metastore-level ABAC policies are in Beta in Unity Catalog. You can now attach an ABAC policy (row filter, column mask, GRANT, or DENY) at the metastore level, so a single policy applies across every catalog in the metastore, including catalogs created later. This gives governance teams one place to enforce organization-wide data protection rules without replicating a policy for each catalog.

For details, see Metastore-level ABAC policies (Beta).

articles.title: Moonshot AI Kimi K2.7 is scheduled for retirement
articles.summary: Moonshot AI Kimi K2.7 will be retired on October 30, 2026. Kimi K3 is the recommended replacement. See Deprecated and retired models for migration guidance.

articles.title: Base environments are now supported on classic compute (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now use base environments to manage Python dependencies on classic compute. You can use Databricks-provided environments or custom workspace-level environments. See Manage dependencies using environments.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Convert a SQL dataset to a local metric view: You can now convert a SQL dataset into a local metric view from the dataset's context menu, and Genie Code handles the conversion. See Local metric views and Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
  • SQL dataset parameters in Genie Code: Genie Code for dashboard authoring now understands SQL dataset parameters when building and editing dashboards. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
  • Reference aggregated field values in widget titles and descriptions: Type @ in a visualization widget's title or description to insert a field reference. The reference shows a live, formatted metric, such as a sum or an average, that responds to the dashboard's filters. Click the reference to change the field, aggregation function, and number or date formatting. See Reference a filter or a field.
  • Default expand level for pivot tables: You can now set the number of row and column hierarchy levels a pivot table expands to when it first loads. See Set the default expand level.
  • Independent axis scaling on faceted charts: You can now scale a numeric axis to each subchart's own data on a faceted chart instead of sharing one range across subcharts. Set the axis range to Per facet. See Faceting.
  • Theme picker previews: The preset theme picker now shows a color palette preview for each theme before you select it.
  • Reorder field variable options: You can now reorder the options in a field variable.
  • Style pivot table totals: You can now style the headers and values of a pivot table's totals independently, and apply conditional styling to them. See Style pivot table totals.
  • Dashboard variable undo and redo fix: Fixed a bug where undo and redo did not apply to dashboard variables.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary: • Multiple files and folders in skills: A Genie One skill can now include multiple files and sub-folders, up to three folders deep and 50 files or folders per skill. Skills can load text files only. See Skills.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Larger PDF uploads: You can now upload PDFs with up to 100 pages to Genie One and Genie Agents, increased from 20. See Upload a file and Upload a file to a Genie Agent.
  • Summarize up to six months of activity: Authors can now summarize up to six months of Genie Agent activity from the Monitor tab. See Review usage and trends.
  • Agents use only attached sources: A Genie Agent now uses only the data assets explicitly attached as sources. See Manage data objects.
  • Fixed Analyze Agent Usage summary: Fixed a bug where Analyze Agent Usage summarized only the last 20 messages sent to the agent.

articles.title: Anthropic models will be removed from AWS GovCloud IL5 workspaces
articles.summary:
On September 19, 2026, Anthropic models will be removed from Databricks on AWS GovCloud and AWS GovCloud DoD workspaces that have the DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) compliance standard selected. After this date, IL5 workspaces can't create or use endpoints that serve Anthropic models. Migrate any affected endpoints to another supported model before September 19, 2026.

See DoD IL5.

For examples and tutorials, see the following:

  • Create and manage providers with Model Provider Services

articles.title: Managed agent memory and sessions are in Beta
articles.summary:
Managed agent memory and managed agent sessions are in Beta. Databricks now provides two fully managed, Lakebase-backed stores for agent state, both usable from agents built on any framework:

  • Managed agent memory gives agents durable, long-term memory that persists across conversations, with semantic search. See Agent memory.
  • Managed agent sessions store durable conversation history that an agent reads at the start of a turn and appends to as it runs. See Agent sessions.

articles.title: Account-only user access to Genie One (Beta)
articles.summary: Genie One now supports account-only users, so users in a registered identity provider can access account-level Genie One without being assigned to a workspace or granted consumer access. When enabled, eligible users are enrolled automatically. Unity Catalog continues to govern what each user can see. See Account-only user access to Genie One.

articles.title: VARIANT cast extends to ARRAY and MAP columns in ABAC column masks
articles.summary: You can now use a single VARIANT function to mask columns of type ARRAY and MAP, in addition to STRUCT and other types. This requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above. See Masking multiple column types with a single function.

articles.title: Webhook-triggered deployments for Databricks Apps will soon be generally available
articles.summary:
Starting in October 2026, webhook-triggered deployments for Databricks Apps will be generally available. Automatically deploy your app when changes are pushed to a connected GitHub or Azure DevOps repository, so your deployed app stays in sync with your repository without manual redeployment.

See Deploy a Databricks app.

articles.title: Automatic change data feed will soon be available in all supported regions
articles.summary:
Automatic change data feed (Auto CDF) is rolling out to workspaces over the next month and will be available in all supported regions by the end of October 2026. Auto CDF computes row-level changes at query time using row tracking, so you don't need to enable change data feed on each Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg v3 table. It requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above with row tracking enabled.

See Automatic change data feed.

articles.title: Lakebase snapshots API (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now manage Lakebase snapshots programmatically. The snapshots API lets you create, get, list, and delete point-in-time snapshots of a project branch, and restore a snapshot by creating a new branch from it. This API is in Beta and available to all Lakebase workspaces. See Create a snapshot.

articles.title: Sharing foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing is now generally available
articles.summary: Sharing and reading foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing is now generally available. Providers can share Delta-format tables federated from OneLake, a Hive metastore, or AWS Glue, without copying data into Databricks. See Add foreign Delta tables to a share.

articles.title: Data Classification now scans Unity Catalog views (Beta)
articles.summary: Data Classification can now scan Unity Catalog views in addition to tables, classifying columns for sensitive data using the same detection engine. This is a Beta feature. See Classify views.

articles.title: JAR tasks on serverless compute will soon be available for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
In early October 2026, running JAR tasks on serverless compute will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Package your Java or Scala Spark code in a JAR and run it as a JAR task on serverless compute in a Lakeflow Job, without provisioning or managing clusters.

See Create and run JARs on serverless compute.

articles.title: Window measures on a numeric index column in metric views
articles.summary: Window measures support unitless offset and trailing/leading ranges on a consecutive integer order column. Use a numeric index for non-calendar periods such as fiscal weeks or 4-4-5 periods. See Window measures on a numeric index column.

articles.title: Genie visualizations in Slack replies (Public Preview)
articles.summary: When a Genie response includes a chart, the visualization now appears as an image in the Slack reply. If you installed the Databricks Genie app for Slack previously, reinstall it to enable this. See Visualizations.

articles.title: The counter_diff SQL window function is now available
articles.summary: The counter_diff window function calculates differences between consecutive cumulative counter values and handles counter resets, for time-series analysis of counter data. It is available in Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime 19 and above. See counter_diff analytic window function.

articles.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway with text and image inputs. See supported regions. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.
