articles.title: Standard performance mode is now available for one-time runs in the Jobs API
articles.summary: You can now set performance_target to STANDARD in the Jobs API. Apache Airflow's DatabricksSubmitRunOperator also supports this. See Create and trigger a one-time run and Select a performance mode.

articles.title: Sharing foreign Iceberg tables with OpenSharing is now generally available
articles.summary: Sharing and reading foreign Iceberg tables with OpenSharing is now generally available. Providers can share Iceberg tables federated from foreign Iceberg catalogs using Lakehouse Federation, including to recipients using external Iceberg clients. See Add foreign Iceberg tables to a share for providers and Read data in a shared foreign Iceberg table for recipients.

articles.title: Sharing foreign schemas and tables with OpenSharing is now generally available
articles.summary:
Sharing and reading foreign schemas and foreign tables with OpenSharing is now generally available. Providers can share foreign schemas and tables federated from external data sources using Lakehouse Federation, without copying data into Databricks. See Add foreign schemas or tables to a share for providers and Read data in a shared foreign table or foreign schema for recipients.

Sharing foreign schemas and tables materializes data on the provider's side, which incurs compute and storage costs. See How do I incur and check OpenSharing costs?.

articles.title: Session restore for serverless jobs is in Public Preview
articles.summary: Restore the Python variables and Spark session from a serverless compute job run into a new interactive notebook, so you can debug a failure or explore results without rerunning the entire job. Databricks captures the snapshot automatically for eligible runs. See Session restore for serverless jobs.

articles.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway with text and image inputs. See supported regions. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Managed tables in Lakeflow pipelines (Beta)
articles.summary:
You can now create managed tables in Lakeflow pipelines and write to them with one or more append flows. This feature is in Beta. You can also use import_checkpoint on an append flow to migrate an existing Structured Streaming workload into a pipeline without reprocessing the source.

See create_table, CREATE TABLE ... FLOW (pipelines), and append_flow.

articles.title: Maintenance windows for continuous pipelines
articles.summary:
You can now set a maintenance window on a continuous Lakeflow pipeline to control when Databricks applies platform updates that require a restart, such as new runtime versions and serverless infrastructure maintenance. Select a day of the week, a start hour, and a time zone, and Databricks starts maintenance only within that one-hour window. Configure the window in the Jobs UI, the Pipelines UI, or the Jobs REST API.

See Manage updates for continuous pipelines.

articles.title: The Databricks Excel Add-in is now generally available
articles.summary:
The Databricks Excel Add-in is now generally available. Connect Microsoft Excel to your Databricks workspace to browse and import governed Unity Catalog tables and views, run SQL queries, build pivot tables, use custom functions, and write data back to Unity Catalog. You can now also enable Live query when building pivot tables to see results as you update the fields.

See Connect to Databricks from Microsoft Excel.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Increased data source limit: Each Genie Agent supports up to 50 tables, views, or metric views as data sources, up from 30. See Technical requirements and limits.
  • Increased conversation limit: Each Genie Agent can store up to 200,000 conversations, up from 10,000. See Technical requirements and limits.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements
articles.summary:
• More Tableau calculations in /importBI: Importing Tableau reports with the /importBI Genie Code command now supports more cases of parameterized calculations. See Import BI files using Genie Code.
  • Relationship-scoped filters (Public Preview): On a dashboard with relationships, each widget now responds only to filters whose dataset is related to it, so a filter no longer affects unrelated charts. See Dashboard relationships.
  • Choose the warehouse for materialization: When you export a dashboard dataset as a materialized view in Unity Catalog, you can now choose which SQL warehouse runs the materialization. See Export a dataset as a materialized view.
  • Scoped starter questions: On a published dashboard, Ask Genie's suggested starter questions are now scoped to the dashboard page and widget you're viewing.
  • Key insights per page: Key insights now generate for each dashboard page. A New insights badge appears only when new insights are available, along with a live-generating indicator.
  • Selected chart as Ask Genie context: On a published dashboard, the Ask Genie input bar now shows the chart you selected as context, so you can ask questions about that specific chart. See Ask Genie about a specific chart.
  • Metric view reuse when building: When building a dashboard, Genie Code now prefers governed metric views over ad-hoc SQL datasets and reuses an existing metric view when one satisfies the request. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
  • Export and import dashboard themes: You can now export a dashboard's theme to a JSON file and import a theme file into another dashboard, so you can reuse or share a theme without editing the dashboard JSON. See Export or import a theme.
  • Line shape control: Line and area charts now have a Line shape control that connects data points with linear, smooth, or stepped lines. See Line shape.
  • Color scale on pivot table text: The pivot table color scale now includes an Apply to setting, so you can paint the color gradient on the cell text as well as the background. See Value-level settings.
  • Path maps from point sequences: Path maps can now connect a sequence of ordered points into a line, from separate longitude and latitude columns or a single point geometry column, in addition to a single geometry line column. Use this for trajectories such as GPS tracks. See Path source.

articles.title: Databricks-provided MCP connectors for Genie One and Genie Code are generally available
articles.summary: Genie One and Genie Code can now use Databricks-provided MCP connectors for Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, Atlassian, Slack, and GitHub to search and act on your company's tools while answering questions. Every connection is governed through Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway, which authorizes each tool call, enforces built-in policies and approval requirements, and logs usage and audit activity. Each user authenticates individually, and OAuth tokens aren't shared. See Connect Genie One to external tools and sources.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Genie Code skills in Genie One (Beta): Genie Code skills now appear and are turned on by default in Genie One. Turn individual skills on or off on the customization page.
  • Backend steering: You can now send steering messages to Genie One while it's answering, so you can guide a response without waiting for it to finish.
  • PowerPoint uploads: You can now upload PowerPoint (.pptx) files to a Genie One conversation. See Upload a file.
  • Memory confirmation prompts (Beta): Genie One can now suggest a memory when it detects a fact worth remembering in your request and asks you to confirm before saving it. Approve, modify, or reject the suggestion. See Add to Genie One's memory.

articles.title: Horizontal scaling for Databricks Apps will soon be available for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
In early October 2026, horizontal scaling for Databricks Apps will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Horizontal scaling lets you run an app across multiple instances behind a single app URL for higher availability and concurrency.

See Horizontal scaling for Databricks apps.

articles.title: Configurable retention for system tables is in Beta
articles.summary: Account admins can now set an account-wide retention period from 30 to 3,650 days for supported system tables. See Configure system table data retention.

articles.title: Genie Code adds conversation controls
articles.summary: Genie Code now includes conversation controls that let you branch and revise a chat. You can fork a conversation into a new, independent thread from a point you choose, ask a quick side question with /btw without adding it to the thread, and edit an earlier message to regenerate the conversation from that point. See Branch and edit Genie Code chats.

articles.title: External secrets in Unity Catalog (Beta)
articles.summary: External secrets connect a Unity Catalog schema to AWS Secrets Manager. The secrets appear in Unity Catalog as read-only securable objects that you govern with Unity Catalog privileges. Databricks reads their values from AWS Secrets Manager on demand. See External secrets in Unity Catalog.

articles.title: Celigo connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Celigo connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector ingests audit log events, such as create, update, and delete operations on resources, from Celigo (integrator.io) into Databricks. Authentication uses a Celigo integrator.io API token.

See Celigo connector.

articles.title: Anysphere Organization connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Anysphere Organization connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector uses the Anysphere (Cursor) Organization Admin API to ingest organization members, groups, and group members into Databricks as daily snapshots. Authentication uses a Cursor Organization Admin API key.

See Anysphere Organization connector.

articles.title: Anaplan connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Anaplan connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector ingests audit trail events and user account records from your Anaplan tenant into Databricks. Authentication uses an Anaplan CA certificate and its paired private key.

See Anaplan connector.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.36 is rolling out in Current
articles.summary: Databricks SQL version 2026.36 is rolling out to the Current channel. See features in 2026.36.

articles.title: The partner-powered AI features setting will be removed
articles.summary:
On November 1, 2026, Databricks will remove the account- and workspace-level toggle for partner-powered AI features. Each workspace will keep its current setting value: if the setting is enabled, it stays enabled, and if it's disabled, it stays disabled. Removing the toggle doesn't change any setting values. After November 1, 2026, to change this setting, contact your Databricks account team.

See Partner-powered AI features.

articles.title: Incremental ingestion for Salesforce formula fields in Lakeflow Connect will soon be generally available
articles.summary:
Incremental ingestion for Salesforce formula fields in Lakeflow Connect will soon be generally available. Today, Lakeflow Connect ingests formula fields by taking a full snapshot on each pipeline run by default. When incremental formula field ingestion is generally available, full snapshots will no longer be the default. Incremental ingestion typically improves performance and reduces cost.

See Ingest Salesforce formula fields incrementally.

articles.title: Lakebase now supports PCI-DSS and HITRUST in all AWS regions
articles.summary: Lakebase is now PCI-DSS and HITRUST compliant in all AWS regions where it is available, for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Previously, this support was limited to the us-east-1 region on AWS. See Data protection.

articles.title: time_bucket SQL function aligns timestamps to fixed-width time buckets
articles.summary:
time_bucket returns the start of the fixed-width interval a timestamp falls into, aligned to an origin you choose (for example, 15-minute or 3-month buckets). Use it instead of date_trunc when the bucket width or start is not a calendar unit.

See time_bucket function.

articles.title: Partner-powered AI features can no longer be disabled in the settings UI
articles.summary:
You can no longer disable the partner-powered AI features setting in the account or workspace settings UI, but can still enable it. Until November 1, 2026, you can still use the Settings API to enable or disable the setting.

On November 1, 2026, the setting will be removed, and any change will then require contacting your Databricks account team.

articles.title: ABAC DENY policies are in Beta
articles.summary:
ABAC DENY policies are in Beta in Unity Catalog. DENY policies can be used to explicitly deny the MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL privilege to prevent specified principals, including object owners, from performing access-management operations. They always take precedence over any grant.

For details, see ABAC DENY policies (Beta).

articles.title: See which chunks support each ai_search answer (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now turn on the generate_citations option in the ai_search function to see which retrieved chunks the model used to support each answer it generates. ai_search function

articles.title: Zerobus Ingest into default storage is now in Public Preview
articles.summary: Ingesting into tables backed by default storage with Zerobus Ingest in Lakeflow Connect is now in Public Preview. See Create or identify the target table.

articles.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway for enterprise reasoning, structured document processing, coding, agentic search, multimodal inputs, and long-context workloads. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway for enterprise reasoning, structured document processing, coding, agentic search, multimodal inputs, and long-context workloads. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token.

articles.title: Share metric views with OpenSharing (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now share metric views with Databricks users in other metastores or accounts using OpenSharing. See Add metric views to a share and Read shared metric views.

articles.title: Environment version 6 is now available
articles.summary: You can now select environment version 6 as your base environment for serverless and standard classic compute. See Environment version 6.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Embedded dashboard filter APIs: In embedded dashboards, you can now set and retrieve filter values through APIs. See Control dashboard filters programmatically.
  • Ranked table calculations in /importBI: Importing reports from Power BI and Tableau with the /importBI Genie Code command now includes ranked table calculations.
  • Color mappings: In a dashboard's theme settings, you can assign a specific color to a value by name. Any visualization that colors by that value uses the assigned color across the dashboard, for both color by field and color by series. See Consistent colors across widgets.
  • Rich text for dynamic data references: You can now apply rich text formatting to dynamic data references in text widgets, widget titles, and descriptions.
  • Dashboard variable improvements: Enhancements to dashboard variables:
    • Multiple fields: Viewers can now add, remove, and swap multiple fields through a dashboard variable on a visualization, instead of switching one field at a time. See Use dashboard variables.
    • Source dataset for options: Dashboard variable options now show their source dataset as a subtitle. See Create a dashboard variable.
  • Metric view downloads respect display names: Downloads from a metric view now use the display names defined for its fields. See Local metric views.
  • Always-visible scrollbars on faceted charts: Scrollbars now stay visible on scrollable faceted charts.
  • Data attachments in Slack and Teams: Dashboard subscriptions delivered to Slack and Microsoft Teams can now include data attachments in CSV, TSV, or Excel format. See Data attachments.
  • Cross-dataset filtering through relationships (Public Preview): When datasets are connected by a relationship, filters, selections, and parameters applied to one dataset now automatically carry across to widgets built on the related datasets. See Create dashboard relationships.
  • Genie Code for dashboard authoring: New authoring capabilities and fixes for Genie Code:
    • Improved automatic widget layout: When Genie Code adds widgets to a dashboard, it now places them in available layout space automatically.
    • Smoother editing: Genie Code no longer appears to stall between edits, and multi-step edits apply with less delay between steps.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• SQL function descriptions: When a SQL function is attached as a tool, you can now view the function's description. See How does Genie use SQL functions?.
  • Upgraded chat-mode models: Genie Agents chat mode now uses upgraded large language models.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Ask Genie button hidden when unsupported: In embedded dashboards, the Ask Genie button is now hidden when it isn't supported. See Ask Genie in embedded dashboards.
  • Push notifications for scheduled tasks (Public Preview): The Genie mobile app can now send push notifications for scheduled tasks to iOS devices. See Push notifications.

articles.title: Web search in Genie One (Beta)
articles.summary: Genie One can now search the public web to answer questions that need current information, such as recent releases, third-party documentation, or news. Genie One decides when to search and cites the sources it uses, showing each as a link you can open. See Search the web.

articles.title: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash now available as a Databricks-hosted model

articles.title: Shared Serverless for Git Folders is in Beta
articles.summary: You can now use Shared Serverless for Git Folders to share serverless compute and a pyproject.toml-managed environment across notebooks and files in a Git folder. See Use Shared Serverless for Git folders and bundles.

articles.title: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash now available as a Databricks-hosted model
articles.summary:

articles.title: AI Search supports struct and map columns and filter-only queries
articles.summary: You can now index and filter struct and map columns in AI Search, and run filter-only queries that return rows matching a filter without vector or keyword retrieval. See Query an AI Search index.

articles.title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 now available as a Databricks-hosted model

articles.title: Apache Arrow support for Zerobus Ingest is now generally available
articles.summary: Apache Arrow support for Zerobus Ingest in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available. See Use Arrow Flight with Zerobus Ingest.

articles.title: Genie One web search is in Beta
articles.summary: Genie One can now search the public web to answer questions that need current information, such as recent release notes, third-party documentation, or news. Genie One cites the external sources it uses as links in its response. See Search the web.

articles.title: Genie One and Genie Agents can now use models served through OpenAI on Databricks
articles.summary: Genie One and Genie Agents can now use models served through OpenAI on Databricks when partner-powered AI features are enabled. For the hosting provider used by each feature, see Hosting provider used when partner-powered AI features setting is enabled and disabled.

articles.title: Genie Code scheduled tasks are now generally available
articles.summary: Genie Code scheduled tasks are now generally available. You can schedule Genie Code to run a prompt on a recurring schedule. Each run executes your prompt as a full Genie Code session and produces a continuable Genie chat with the results, so you can turn recurring analysis and other work into an unattended background task. Create a scheduled task by asking Genie Code in chat or from the Schedules menu. See Genie Code scheduled tasks.

articles.title: Databricks Runtime 19: September 1, 2026
articles.summary:
New features and improvements

  • Automatic change data feed is generally available: Automatic change data feed (Auto CDF) computes row-level changes at query time using row tracking, without requiring you to manually enable change data feed on each Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg v3 table. Auto CDF removes write-time overhead and makes MERGE and UPDATE operations about 15% faster on tables that you query for changes. It works with batch queries, Structured Streaming, and Delta Sharing, and requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above with row tracking enabled. See Automatic change data feed.
  • variant_strip_nulls function: SQL and the Scala and Python DataFrame APIs now support variant_strip_nulls, which recursively removes object fields whose values are variant nulls.
  • parse_sql function: The new parse_sql function parses a SQL statement and returns structured JSON containing statement metadata, table references, select-list expressions, or parser error information.

Behavioral changes

  • from_protobuf skips malformed unselected fields when schema pruning is enabled: When protobuf schema pruning is enabled, from_protobuf no longer decodes or validates fields that a query does not select. A malformed unselected field no longer nulls the row in PERMISSIVE mode or fails the query in FAILFAST mode.
  • JDBC pushdown correctly handles null literals: Data Source v2 JDBC pushdown now emits the SQL NULL literal instead of the string 'null'. Queries that group expressions such as NULLIF now produce a null group instead of a separate 'null' string group.
  • HTTP and AI functions no longer follow redirects: http_request and AI functions no longer follow HTTP 3xx redirects. Calls that receive a redirect now return a remote HTTP failure for the redirect status. File-source connector downloads are unaffected.

Library and environment updates

This release restores JupyterLab and notebook-related Python libraries to the standard runtime environment to resolve an issue that prevented ipywidgets from rendering in notebook cells. The Python library changes are:

articles.title: Pipeline events system table is in Beta
articles.summary:
The pipeline_events system table is in Beta. This table records Lakeflow pipelines event log entries for pipelines in your account, capturing lifecycle transitions, flow progress, data quality metrics, errors, and other operational data across all pipelines and workspaces in a region. Use it to query historical pipeline activity, build alerts on pipeline failures, and correlate pipeline behavior with other Lakeflow system tables.

See Pipeline events system table reference.

articles.title: ABAC GRANT policies are generally available for models and services
articles.summary: ABAC GRANT policies for models, model services, model provider services, and model context protocol (MCP) services are now generally available. These policies dynamically grant Unity Catalog privileges to securable objects whose governed tags match a condition, instead of granting privileges on each object individually. See ABAC GRANT policies.

articles.title: Nanosecond-precision timestamps (Beta)
articles.summary:
You can now use TIMESTAMP(9) and TIMESTAMP_NTZ(9) for nanosecond-precision timestamps in Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime 19 and above.

See TIMESTAMP type and TIMESTAMP_NTZ type.

articles.title: Zhipu AI GLM 5.3 now available as a Databricks-hosted model
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports GLM 5.3 as a Databricks-hosted model in supported US and Americas regions. This text-only mixture of experts (MoE) model supports a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens, up to 65,536 output tokens, function calling, structured output, coding, agentic tool use, and always-on reasoning. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Restrict service principal OAuth secrets to specific API scopes
articles.summary: You can now restrict a service principal's OAuth secret to specific API scopes, such as sql or jobs, instead of all APIs. A token minted from a scoped secret can't exceed those scopes, which limits the impact of a leaked secret. See Authorize service principal access to Databricks with OAuth.

This text-only mixture of experts (MoE) model supports a context window of up to 1,048,576 tokens, up to 65,536 output tokens, function calling, structured output, coding, agentic tool use, and always-on reasoning. articles.title: ai_transcribe function (Beta)
articles.summary:
The ai_transcribe() SQL function transcribes an audio file into text. It returns the transcript as time-stamped segments, and labels each segment with a speaker when speaker diarization is enabled for your workspace. The output is a VARIANT value, so you can chain it into other AI Functions. This feature is in Beta.

See ai_transcribe function.

articles.title: Monitor and cap external provider costs
articles.summary:
Unity Gateway can now track and cap spend on external model providers, such as Amazon Bedrock and Azure AI Foundry, not just Databricks-provided models. If your organization already has capacity commitments directly with a provider, Unity Gateway becomes the single point to track that usage and enforce spend limits across teams and use cases. To turn it on, enable External Model Spend in Budgets (Beta) on the account console Previews page, then select Include external model usage when you create a budget scoped to the Unity Gateway resource type.

See Include external model usage.

articles.title: Unity Catalog Skills (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now publish, govern, and share agent skills with Unity Catalog. A skill is a first-class Unity Catalog securable (catalog.schema.skill) that follows the SKILL.md specification, so you register it once and control who can discover, use, and update it with the same permissions, tags, and audit that protect your tables. Coding agents download published skills or load them live over MCP. See Skills support in Unity Gateway.

articles.title: Monitor and cap external provider costs
articles.summary:
Unity Gateway can now track and cap spend on external model providers, such as Amazon Bedrock and Azure AI Foundry, not just Databricks-provided models. If your organization already has capacity commitments directly with a provider, Unity Gateway becomes the single point to track that usage and enforce spend limits across teams and use cases. To turn it on, enable External Model Spend in Budgets (Beta) on the account console Previews page, then select Include external model usage when you create a budget scoped to the Unity Gateway resource type.

See Include external model usage.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Hide pages in published dashboards: Dashboard authors can now hide a page so that it doesn't appear when the dashboard is published, while keeping it in the dashboard for authors. See Hide a page in published dashboards.
  • Path maps: You can now use the path map visualization to show routes and connections between locations on a map. See Map visualizations.
  • Table column header alignment: You can now set left, center, or right alignment for table column headers, independent of the cell alignment. See Field-level settings.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Agent mode APIs: The Agent mode APIs for Genie Agents are now generally available. Run Agent mode programmatically to integrate it into your own applications, such as chatbots, scheduled reports, and internal tools. See the Agent mode API reference.
  • Unity Catalog functions as agent tools: Agent authors can now attach both scalar and table-valued Unity Catalog functions as tools for a Genie Agent. See How does Genie use SQL functions?.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Open Unity Catalog tables in Genie: You can now open Unity Catalog tables directly in Genie without navigating to Catalog Explorer. See Open tables.
    • Tables in chat: Opening a table from chat keeps you in the conversation. View overview details, columns, and sample data next to your chat.
    • Tables in Discover: Opening a table from Discover shows a full-page catalog-style view optimized for Genie.
    • Ask Genie: From a table in Discover, click Ask Genie to start a chat about that table.
    • Request access: If you only have browse access, you can request access from the table view.
  • Pin chats: You can now pin a chat in the Genie One sidebar to keep it at the top for quick access. See Manage chats in the sidebar.
  • Rename chats: You can now rename a chat in the Genie One sidebar. See Manage chats in the sidebar.
  • Visualizations in scheduled task emails: Scheduled task email outputs can now include visualizations. See Scheduled tasks.
  • Genie One desktop app (Beta): The Genie One desktop app, a native macOS app, is now available. Chat with your data and work with Genie without a browser. See Use Genie One on desktop.
  • Create scheduled tasks in the Genie mobile app (Public Preview): You can now create scheduled tasks directly from the Genie mobile app. See Scheduled tasks.

articles.title: Lakeflow Designer August Release
articles.summary:
The Lakeflow Designer August release adds the Unique operator, expands the Aggregate, Select, and Python operators, and improves the canvas, preview, and version-history experience. The following updates are now available:

  • Unique operator: Use the new Unique operator to remove duplicate rows, optionally keying on a subset of columns and ordering the rows to control which duplicate is kept. See Unique.
  • Count distinct: The Aggregate operator now supports a COUNT DISTINCT function to count the unique values in a column. See Aggregate.
  • Dynamic column selection: The Select operator can now choose columns dynamically by data type, name pattern, or formula, so the output adapts as the input schema changes. See Select.
  • Python preview mode: The Python operator can run different code during previews than during full runs by checking config["is_preview"], so you can skip side effects such as writes and notifications while previewing. See Python preview mode.
  • Streaming Python output: Python operator output now streams into the output pane as the operator runs, so you can see results before the run finishes. See Python.
  • Enable and disable operators and groups: Disable individual operators or entire groups to exclude them from runs, then enable them again when you need them. See Group.
  • Operator lineage highlighting: Select an operator to highlight its lineage from upstream sources to downstream sinks on the canvas. See Operators.
  • Run all: Run every operator in the visual data prep at the same time with the new Run all button. See Run the full visual data prep.
  • Exact row count for each operator: You can now see the exact row count for each operator. Preview an operator with Rows scanned: All rows to show its exact output row count beneath the operator on the canvas. See Control how much data previews process.
  • Apply results-table changes to the canvas as operators: Filter and transform your data directly in the output table. After renaming, filtering, or inserting a column in the output table, click Apply to canvas to create operators that reproduce exactly what you did in the results table. See Transform data directly in the results table.
  • Load more filter values: When you use the Filter operator, you can now load more of a column's values on demand instead of only a sample. See Filter.
  • @ mention menu for columns and functions: Type @ in an expression editor to search the operator's input columns and the built-in SQL functions, then insert the one you want. See Custom columns.
  • Visual canvas diff in version history: Version history now shows a visual diff on the canvas, highlighting the operators that were added, removed, or changed between versions. See Review version history.

articles.title: Genie Code is now available as a Lakeflow Jobs task (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now run prompts with Genie Code as a task in a Lakeflow Job. Genie Code runs your prompt autonomously. It can read upstream task outputs and call tools as needed. The task returns a link to the resulting Genie Code conversation with its response. See Genie Code task for jobs.

articles.title: Genie Code for AI Runtime (Public Preview)
articles.summary: Use Genie Code to develop and troubleshoot deep learning workloads in notebooks connected to AI Runtime. Now in Public Preview, it generates distributed training code, resolves environment and dependency issues, and debugs GPU and distributed workload failures. See Use Genie Code with AI Runtime.

articles.title: Share foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing (Public Preview)
articles.summary: You can now use OpenSharing to share foreign Delta tables, which are Delta-format tables registered in a foreign catalog such as OneLake, a Hive metastore, or AWS Glue. Providers add foreign Delta tables to a share, and recipients access the shared data in read-only format. See Add foreign Delta tables to a share and Read data in a shared foreign Delta table.

articles.title: Atlassian Audit Logs connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Atlassian Audit Logs connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector ingests organization audit log events, such as user, security, and configuration changes, from Atlassian into Databricks. Authentication uses an Atlassian organization API key.

See Atlassian Audit Logs connector.

articles.title: AI Functions REST API is now generally available
articles.summary: You can now call ai_parse_document, ai_extract, and ai_classify through the AI Functions REST API. See intelligent document processing for more details.

articles.title: Zhipu AI GLM 5.3 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
Zhipu AI GLM 5.3 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway for multimodal reasoning, coding, and agentic workloads. Access it through the same governed API as other models, with centralized permissions, guardrails, spend controls, and observability, and switch models without changing application code.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

To query the model and see supported regions, see Use foundation models.

articles.title: xAI Grok 4.6 is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
xAI Grok 4.6 is now available on Unity Gateway for reasoning-heavy coding and agentic workflows. Access it through the same governed API as other models, with centralized permissions, guardrails, spend controls, and observability, and switch models without changing application code.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

To query the model and see supported regions, see Use foundation models.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Chat mode in Genie One: You can now submit prompts to a Genie Agent in Chat mode from Genie One.
  • Cancel Agent mode responses through the API: You can now cancel in-progress Agent mode responses through the API. See the Cancel Genie agent response API.
  • Download visualizations API: Retrieving visualization results through the Genie Conversation API is now generally available. See the Conversation API reference.

articles.title: Zerobus Ingest into streaming tables is now generally available
articles.summary: Ingesting into streaming tables with Zerobus Ingest in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available. Writing to a streaming table works the same way as writing to a managed Delta table, with the same limits and quotas. See Create or identify the target table.

articles.title: Query text is now masked by default in system tables and APIs
articles.summary:
Because SQL statements can contain sensitive information, Databricks now masks query text in the following places:

  • statement_text in system.query.history returns <REDACTED>.
  • query_text in the Query History API and the List Queries API returns <REDACTED>.
  • Keys in request_params in system.access.audit that contain SQL definitions are omitted.

Account admins and members of the databricks_pii_access account group can read unmasked query text. To grant access, an account admin creates the group and adds members. See Create and manage the databricks_pii_access group. For details about the masked fields, see Access masked statement text and Access masked request parameters.

articles.title: xAI Grok 4.6 is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
xAI Grok 4.6 is now available on Unity Gateway for reasoning-heavy coding and agentic workflows. Access it through the same governed API as other models, with centralized permissions, guardrails, spend controls, and observability, and switch models without changing application code.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

To query the model and see supported regions, see Use foundation models.

articles.title: Zhipu AI GLM 5.3 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
Zhipu AI GLM 5.3 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway for multimodal reasoning, coding, and agentic workloads. Access it through the same governed API as other models, with centralized permissions, guardrails, spend controls, and observability, and switch models without changing application code.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

To query the model and see supported regions, see Use foundation models.

articles.title: LTAP Direct Writes accelerates synced table loads (Beta)
articles.summary: LTAP Direct Writes speeds up how synced tables load into Lakebase. When you create a synced table, Lakebase loads a full copy of your Unity Catalog data into your Postgres branch. LTAP Direct Writes accelerates that initial load and full refreshes by writing directly to the storage layer instead of through your compute endpoint, so large loads finish faster without competing with your queries. It's supported on projects running Postgres 16, 17, or 18, and you opt in when you create the synced table. See Serve lakehouse data with synced tables.

articles.title: The Genie One desktop app for macOS is in Beta
articles.summary: The Genie One desktop app is now in Beta. The native macOS app opens Genie One on your desktop instead of in a browser tab, so business users can chat with data in natural language, work with their threads and documents, and use Genie Agents without a browser. See Use Genie One on desktop.

articles.title: Anysphere Audit Logs connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Anysphere Audit Logs connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector uses the Anysphere (Cursor) Admin API to incrementally ingest team audit-log events into Databricks. Authentication uses a Cursor Admin API key.

See Anysphere Audit Logs connector.

articles.title: ai_prep_search supports plain text and markdown input (Beta)
articles.summary:
The ai_prep_search() SQL function now accepts plain text and markdown STRING content in addition to the structured VARIANT output of ai_parse_document. You can now chunk and prepare text that you already have as a string for AI Search indexing and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, without first running it through document parsing.

See ai_prep_search function.

articles.title: ai_parse_document quality improvements: checkboxes, handwriting, and figure text
articles.summary: ai_parse_document further improves checkbox extraction and handling of strikethrough text and handwriting. It also improves extraction of text from figures. See ai_parse_document function.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.35 is now available in Preview
articles.summary:
Databricks SQL version 2026.35 is now available in the Preview channel. Review the following section to learn about new features and behavioral changes.

Aggregate arrays with collect_union

The collect_union aggregate function returns the distinct union of the elements in arrays within each group.

HAVING is evaluated before window functions in queries with generators

For queries that include generators, such as explode, window functions are now evaluated after the HAVING filter. Window results include only the rows that HAVING retains.

Policy logic is hidden in query plans by default

Query plans no longer expose row filter and column mask policy logic unless the user has the INSPECT_POLICY_EXECUTION metastore privilege. See Row filters and column masks.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW preserves metadata atomically

For Unity Catalog views, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW now performs an atomic replacement that preserves the view identity, grants, tags, and comments by default. Governed tag protections continue to apply.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.32 is rolling out in Current
articles.summary: Databricks SQL version 2026.32 is rolling out to the Current channel. See features in 2026.32.

articles.title: August 24, 2026
articles.summary:
This serverless compute release includes updates from Databricks Runtime 19.

New features

  • collect_union aggregate function: The collect_union aggregate function returns the distinct union of the elements in arrays within each group.

Behavior changes

  • HAVING is evaluated before window functions in queries with generators: For queries that include generators, such as explode, window functions are now evaluated after the HAVING filter. Window results therefore include only rows retained by HAVING.

  • Policy logic is hidden in query plans by default: Query plans no longer expose row filter and column mask policy logic unless the user has the INSPECT_POLICY_EXECUTION metastore privilege.

  • Delta API DML uses policy-definer rights: DeltaTable.delete, DeltaTable.update, and DeltaTable.merge now resolve row filter and column mask policy functions with the policy definer's rights, matching SQL DML. Callers no longer need EXECUTE on those policy functions when they have the required table permissions.

articles.title: Secrets in Unity Catalog will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Secrets in Unity Catalog will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in late September 2026.

Store, govern, and access secrets as securable objects in Unity Catalog. A Unity Catalog secret uses the three-level namespace (catalog.schema.secret) and is governed by Unity Catalog privileges, so you can apply the same access controls and auditing that you use for other data assets.

See Secrets in Unity Catalog.

articles.title: Postgres minor version updates
articles.summary: Lakebase updated its supported Postgres versions to 16.15, 17.11, and 18.6. These minor releases bring you the latest upstream Postgres fixes and security patches. When a new minor version is available, Lakebase applies it the next time your compute restarts. See Manage updates.

articles.title: Genie Code is now available in the Lakebase project UI
articles.summary: A new Genie entry in the Lakebase project sidebar opens Genie Code, the agentic Databricks assistant, scoped to your Lakebase project. Ask it in natural language to run multi-step data and AI tasks: explore your databases and tables, investigate and debug issues, and create and populate tables. It's the same Genie Code you use elsewhere in Databricks, here working on your Lakebase project, and it's now available for all Lakebase projects. See Genie Code.

articles.title: Unity Gateway now supports Provisioned Throughput
articles.summary:
Govern Provisioned Throughput (PT) traffic through Unity Gateway, bringing PT models under the same access controls, usage tracking, rate limits, payload logging, and guardrails as other model traffic.

See AI governance with Unity Gateway.

articles.summary:
Library and environment updates

  • Updated Java from Zulu21.50+19-CA to Zulu21.52+15-CA.
  • Updated Java libraries:
    • com.fasterxml.jackson.core.jackson-annotations from 2.21 to 2.22

articles.title: Verkada connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Verkada connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector ingests organization audit logs and access users from your Verkada organization into Databricks. Authentication uses a Verkada organization API key.

See Verkada connector.

articles.title: Unity Gateway now supports Provisioned Throughput
articles.summary:
Govern Provisioned Throughput (PT) traffic through Unity Gateway, bringing PT models under the same access controls, usage tracking, rate limits, payload logging, and guardrails as other model traffic.

See AI governance with Unity Gateway.

articles.title: Private network gateway is in Private Preview
articles.summary: Private network gateway is in Private Preview. A private network gateway connects Databricks serverless compute to resources in your VPC, on-premises systems, and the internet through a single managed gateway, reusing your existing network connectivity configuration (NCC). Use it for broad private connectivity without onboarding each resource individually, to route serverless egress through your own security appliances for content inspection, or to send egress from a stable set of IP addresses. See Private network gateway.

articles.title: Connect to the Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams with your workspace URL (Public Preview)
articles.summary: When you sign in to the Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams, you can now enter your workspace URL instead of a server hostname to connect to your Databricks account. See Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams.

articles.title: The INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges are in Beta
articles.summary:
The INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges are in Beta in Unity Catalog. These privileges are least-privilege alternatives to MODIFY that let you grant write access to a table's data without also granting the ability to change its schema or other metadata.

The privileges require Databricks Runtime 18.1 or above.

For details, see Fine-grained DML privileges.

articles.title: Upcoming end of life for the Supervisor API
articles.summary:
The Supervisor API (Beta) reaches end of life on September 30, 2026. After that date, the API is no longer available.

Databricks recommends migrating to custom agents on Databricks Apps.

See Supervisor API (deprecated).

articles.title: Monitor all AI activity with the unified trace table (Beta)
articles.summary:
The unified trace table is in Beta. It captures every request and response across your Unity Gateway services into one Unity Catalog table in OpenTelemetry format, giving you a single place to monitor, debug, secure, and audit all AI activity.

See Monitor all AI activity using the unified trace table.

articles.title: Monitor all AI activity with the unified trace table (Beta)
articles.summary:
The unified trace table is in Beta. It captures every request and response across your Unity Gateway services into one Unity Catalog table in OpenTelemetry format, giving you a single place to monitor, debug, secure, and audit all AI activity.

See Monitor all AI activity using the unified trace table.

articles.title: Default Python package repositories are GA for Lakeflow pipelines and classic compute
articles.summary: Configuring default Python package repositories is now generally available for Lakeflow pipelines and for classic compute created via the UI and API. Workspace admins can set private or authenticated registries as the workspace default for these workloads. See Configure default package repositories.

articles.title: Context attributes in ABAC column mask and row filter policies (Beta)
articles.summary:
Context attributes for attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies are in Beta. You can now write Unity Catalog ABAC policy conditions that target the context of a request, such as which OAuth application is calling (request.client_id) and whether the request runs on behalf of a user (request.is_on_behalf_of). The has_context_attribute and has_context_attribute_value functions are supported in the WHEN clause of row filter and column mask policies.

A common use is to restrict the data an agent reads on a user's behalf when it connects through a registered OAuth application, while the user can still read the full data when they query it directly in the workspace.

See Context attribute functions (Beta).

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Import from Power BI and Tableau: Importing reports and data models from Power BI and Tableau with Genie Code (/importBI) is now generally available. See Import BI files using Genie Code.
  • Larger Excel downloads: You can now download up to 1 million rows from a dashboard widget to Excel (.xlsx), up from 100,000. See Download results.
  • Multi-select and move widgets: Dashboard authors can now select multiple widgets and move them together on the canvas by holding Cmd or Ctrl while clicking. See Keyboard shortcuts.
  • Full-width tables in text widgets: Markdown tables in text widgets now use the full width of the widget instead of a fixed width.
  • Hide the sparkline and date labels on counters: You can now hide the sparkline and date labels on counter widgets. See Hide date labels and the sparkline.
  • Consistent colors across widgets: Charts that color by a categorical field now use the same color for the same value across every widget on a dashboard. See Consistent colors across widgets.
  • Duplicate subscriber prevention in the API: Dashboard subscription APIs now prevent duplicate recipients from being added.
  • Unsubscribe removes duplicate subscriptions: Unsubscribing from a schedule by email or from the dashboard now removes all duplicate subscriptions for that recipient. See Manage scheduled dashboard updates and subscriptions.
  • Local metric views: Local metric views are now generally available. Define fields, measures, and join relationships directly in an AI/BI dashboard with a visual interface, without first publishing them to Unity Catalog. See Local metric views.
  • Low-code UI for Unity Catalog metric views in dashboards: When you add a Unity Catalog metric view to a dashboard, it now uses the same low-code UI as local metric views, replacing the legacy UI. You can edit the metric view in Unity Catalog, or extend it locally to add dashboard-specific measures and fields. Unity Catalog metric views that use parameters can't be extended. See Extend a Unity Catalog metric view.
  • Genie Code for dashboard authoring: New authoring capabilities and fixes for Genie Code:
    • Undo and redo: You can now undo and redo edits made by Genie Code. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
    • Materialize datasets: Genie Code can now optionally materialize datasets.
    • Manage email schedules: You can now manage dashboard email schedules directly from Genie Code.
    • Set a schedule's tabular attachment: Genie Code can now set a schedule's tabular attachment, so a scheduled email includes widget data. See Data attachments.
    • Improved layout placement: Genie Code now places widgets in appropriate locations instead of leaving large gaps in the dashboard layout. See Dashboard layout and organization.
    • Visualization title fix: Fixed a bug where visualization title text overlapped the action icons in a Genie Code chat response.
  • Choropleth map fix: Fixed a bug that caused choropleth maps to crash when filtered results returned no data.
  • Waterfall cross-filtering fix: Fixed a bug where waterfall charts did not trigger cross-filtering.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Scheduled task consistency: Scheduled tasks now look up past runs to keep run-to-run outputs consistent. See Scheduled tasks.
  • Export documents to PDF: You can now export Genie One documents to PDF. See Documents in Genie One.
  • Genie mobile (Public Preview): Enhancements to the Genie mobile app:
    • Switch workspaces without signing out: You can now switch between workspaces from within the app instead of signing out and back in. See Switch workspaces.
    • Sign in behind account-level IP access lists: If you were blocked at mobile sign-in by an account-level IP access list, you can now sign in. If your workspace is restricted to your corporate network, off-network devices still need to reach it through that network, such as with a VPN or a managed device.

articles.title: Salesforce connector mTLS authentication is now generally available
articles.summary: Mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for the Salesforce connector in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available. With mTLS, Databricks and Salesforce exchange and verify client certificates to establish two-way trust, combined with the OAuth client credentials flow. Choose it for API-only users or when your organization requires mTLS. See Mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication.

articles.title: Performance mode now applies to materialized view and streaming table refreshes from dbt tasks
articles.summary:
The job-level performance mode setting now propagates to materialized view and streaming table refreshes triggered by dbt tasks. You can set these jobs to Standard mode to optimize for cost, or keep the default Performance-optimized mode for faster startup. Previously, dbt tasks always ran refreshes in Performance-optimized mode.

Standard mode can increase refresh startup latency from under a minute to four to six minutes in exchange for lower compute costs. This change affects only refreshes that materialize as an materialized view or streaming table, so most dbt projects, which create regular tables, are unaffected.

See Select a performance mode for scheduled refreshes.

articles.title: Write data back to Databricks from Google Sheets
articles.summary: The Databricks Connector for Google Sheets now lets you write data from Google Sheets back to a Unity Catalog table. You can create a new table or overwrite an existing table without leaving Google Sheets. See Write data back to Databricks from Google Sheets.

articles.title: Role-based access control (RBAC) will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Role-based access control (RBAC) will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in mid-September 2026.

RBAC lets users assume a role in Databricks. When a user assumes a role, only that role's permissions apply, rather than the user's accumulated permissions. This enables exclusive access. Users must actively assume a role to access sensitive data, preventing them from accessing it under their own identity and from mixing data across use cases, clinical trials, projects, or clients.

See Role-based access control (RBAC).

articles.title: Role-based access control (RBAC) is generally available
articles.summary:
Role-based access control (RBAC) is now generally available. RBAC lets users assume a role in Databricks. When a user assumes a role, only that role's permissions apply, rather than the user's accumulated permissions. This enables exclusive access. Users must actively assume a role to access sensitive data, preventing them from accessing it under their own identity and from mixing data across use cases, clinical trials, projects, or clients.

To enable RBAC, an account admin must turn on the feature at the account level. Workspace admins then enable it in each workspace.

See Role-based access control (RBAC).

articles.title: Choose an effort level in Genie Code
articles.summary: You can now set the effort level for Genie Code to balance response quality and cost. Auto (default) gives you the highest quality responses. For simpler tasks, select Low to use a faster, lower-cost model. See Select a level of effort.

articles.title: ai_extract precision mode is now generally available
articles.summary: You can now use ai_extract precision mode for advanced extraction workloads, including multi-page documents, schemas with 50 or more fields, many extracted items per document, and complex conditional field logic. See ai_extract function.

articles.title: User authorization for Databricks Apps will soon be available for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
In late September 2026, user authorization for Databricks Apps will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. User authorization allows apps to act with the identity of the app user, so apps can access resources on the user's behalf while enforcing the user's existing permissions.

See User authorization.

articles.title: August 17, 2026
articles.summary:
This serverless compute release includes updates from Databricks Runtime 19.

New features

  • is_valid_variant function: The is_valid_variant function returns true if the input is a well-formed VARIANT value and false otherwise. Use it to validate variant data before downstream processing.

  • DataFrameGroupBy.cov and SeriesGroupBy.describe in pandas API on Spark: The pandas API on Spark now supports DataFrameGroupBy.cov, which computes the pairwise covariance of columns within each group, and SeriesGroupBy.describe, which generates descriptive statistics for each group.

  • pa.ChunkedArray support in createDataFrame: createDataFrame() now handles pandas DataFrames with PyArrow ChunkedArray columns, preventing type errors when you use Arrow-backed pandas data.

articles.title: Upcoming deprecation of the data quality monitoring downstream_impact column
articles.summary:
The downstream_impact column in the data quality monitoring results system table is being deprecated.

Deprecation begins September 7, 2026, and rolls out gradually across regions over the following week. Until the rollout reaches your workspace, you might still be able to query downstream_impact. After deprecation completes, the column is no longer populated.

For the affected column, see Data quality monitoring results system table reference and Review anomaly detection logged results.

articles.title: Upcoming deprecation of the data quality monitoring root_cause_analysis column
articles.summary:
The root_cause_analysis column in the data quality monitoring results system table is being deprecated.

Deprecation begins August 18, 2026, and rolls out gradually across regions over the following several days. Until the rollout reaches your workspace, you might still be able to query root_cause_analysis. After deprecation completes, the column is no longer populated.

For the affected column, see Data quality monitoring results system table reference and Review anomaly detection logged results.

articles.title: Manage project environments with %uv commands
articles.summary: You can now use %uv init, %uv add, and %uv sync in serverless notebooks running environment version 5 or above to create a Python project, add dependencies, and sync its environment. See Create reproducible project environments with %uv.

articles.title: Session restore for serverless jobs is now in Beta
articles.summary: Restore the Python variables and Spark session from a serverless compute job run into a new interactive notebook, so you can debug a failure or explore results without rerunning the job. Databricks automatically captures a state snapshot when an eligible run fails, runs 30 minutes or longer, or is cancelled, and keeps it for 7 days after the run completes. This feature is in Beta. See Session restore for serverless jobs.

articles.title: Identity attributes in ABAC column mask policies (Beta)
articles.summary:
Identity attributes are in Beta. You can now write Unity Catalog ABAC column mask policy conditions that target users by attributes synced from your identity provider, such as department or country, in addition to group membership. The has_identity_attribute_value and has_identity_attribute_tag_match functions are supported in the WHEN clause of column mask policies.

See identity attributes.

articles.title: Workiva connector (Beta)

The connector ingests audit activity, users, and roles from your Workiva organization into Databricks. Authentication uses Workiva OAuth2 client credentials.

See Workiva connector.

articles.title: Sharing managed Iceberg tables is now generally available

articles.title: Block or redact sensitive data in requests and responses
articles.summary:
The Sensitive Data Detection guardrail (Beta) detects structured sensitive data (such as Social Security numbers, credit card numbers, IBANs, and phone numbers) and either blocks the interaction or redacts the matched values in place. Detection is deterministic (regular expressions plus checksums and context keywords, with no evaluator model), so it adds under 50 ms for a 100-turn conversation and returns the same result every time. To use it, enable the Enhanced Unity Gateway preview on the account console Previews page.

This release also includes the following improvements:

  • Blocked interactions now return a standard HTTP 200 response with the block reason, instead of a 4xx error, so coding agents that resend history don't re-trigger the same block every turn.
  • Built-in LLM-as-a-judge guardrails can now evaluate a window of recent conversation turns, or the entire conversation history, instead of only the latest message.
  • A new execution flow view shows the order in which guardrails run, end to end.

See Detect sensitive data with a service policy.

articles.title: Smart Routing: Cut AI costs by routing each task to the right model
articles.summary:
Smart Routing (Beta) automatically picks the right model and agent harness for each task, based on complexity, permissions, and budget. It shifts routine work to lower-cost models and reserves frontier models for hard problems, and every routing decision is visible and auditable. Smart Routing works with Claude Code and Codex when you run them through the Unity Gateway CLI or Omnigent, and routes across both proprietary and open models. Only Omnigent can route across coding harnesses, not just models. In internal benchmarks, it matched frontier-level quality while cutting overall task cost by more than 30%.

See Select models or use Smart Routing.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Remove duplicate subscribers: Dashboard authors can now remove duplicate subscribers from a dashboard schedule. See Manage scheduled dashboard updates and subscriptions.
  • Duplicate schedule emails fix: Fixed a bug where dashboard schedules could send duplicate emails to the same subscriber.
  • Import BI filters fix: Fixed a bug where some filters were not created when importing Power BI and Tableau reports with Genie Code (/importBI). See Import BI files using Genie Code.
  • Reversed y-axis tooltip order fix: Fixed a bug where tooltips for line and area charts with a reversed y-axis listed their series in the wrong order.
  • Pivot table None transform fix: Fixed a bug where the None transform on pivot table values produced empty values.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Content search for attached volumes (Beta): For better latency and accuracy when answering questions across larger volumes, you can now optionally enable content search on attached volumes. Content search indexes and prepares your files for the Genie Agent. See How content search works.
  • Analyze files in volumes without Unity Gateway (Beta): Analyzing files in volumes no longer requires Unity Gateway to be enabled. See Analyze files in volumes with a Genie Agent.
  • Send a prompt with an uploaded file: Uploading a file to a conversation no longer automatically sends a message. You can now send a prompt along with the uploaded file. See Upload a file to a Genie Agent.
  • Conversation list API matches monitoring sources: The conversation list API now returns conversations from the public API, Genie One, and embedded Genie, so the conversations it returns match the history shown on the monitoring page. See Use the Genie Agents API.
  • Conversation timestamps in the API: The public Genie Agents API now returns create_time and update_time for a Genie space. GET requests to list or get spaces return the same last-modified information shown in the Genie Agent UI. See Use the Genie Agents API.
  • Metric view synonyms fix: Fixed a bug where synonyms defined in a metric view were not used as context for the agent.
  • Table access error message: Simplified the error message shown when a user does not have access to one or more tables attached to a Genie Agent.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Ontology snippets now available to all customers (Public Preview): Ontology snippets in the Genie Ontology are now available to all customers. Customers no longer need to request access. See Genie Ontology.
  • Workspace instructions: Workspace-level instructions for chat in Genie One are now generally available. See Add workspace instructions for chat.
  • Upload images and Word documents: Genie One now supports uploading images (PNG, JPG, and JPEG) and Word (.docx) files to a conversation, in addition to CSV and Excel files. See Upload a file.
  • MCP writes (Beta): Genie One now supports MCP writes, so connected MCP tools can perform write actions. See Connect Genie One to external tools and sources.
  • PDF attachments for scheduled tasks: Scheduled tasks can now send their results as a PDF email attachment. See Scheduled tasks.
  • Updated Genie Agents terminology: References to "Genie spaces" that remained in the Genie One interface now use the current Genie Agents terminology.

articles.title: SQL alert task in Lakeflow Jobs is now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:

Use the task to evaluate a Databricks SQL alert as part of a Lakeflow Job. The task returns its evaluation state as a task output value, so downstream tasks can branch on the result.

See SQL alert task for jobs.

articles.title: SendGrid connector (Beta)

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.32 is now available in Preview
articles.summary:
Databricks SQL version 2026.32 is now available in the Preview channel. Review the following section to learn about new features and improvements.

Validate VARIANT values with is_valid_variant

The is_valid_variant function returns true when its input is a well-formed VARIANT value and false otherwise. Use it to validate variant data before downstream processing. See Query variant data.

INSERT INTO ... REPLACE for upsert-style writes

INSERT INTO now supports REPLACE USING (<columns>) and REPLACE ON <condition> clauses, which replace existing rows that match on the specified columns or condition. See INSERT.

Scalar UDFs as table-valued function arguments

You can now pass scalar user-defined functions (UDFs) as arguments to table-valued functions. See Table-valued function (TVF) invocation.

articles.title: ABAC GRANT policies now cover Unity Gateway resource types (Beta)
articles.summary:
Attribute-based access control (ABAC) GRANT policies dynamically grant Unity Catalog privileges to securables whose governed tags match a condition. They now support model services, model provider services, Model Context Protocol (MCP) services, and agent services, which are the resource types Unity Gateway governs. This lets you grant access to gateway resources by tag instead of one at a time. All supported types are in Beta.

See ABAC GRANT policies.

articles.title: REPLACE USING flows for standalone streaming tables (Beta)
articles.summary:
REPLACE USING flows are now available for standalone streaming tables in Beta.

Use a REPLACE USING flow when your source is a series of partial snapshots keyed by column. On each update, the flow replaces all rows that match the specified key columns and leaves all other rows unchanged. A SEQUENCE BY column orders the updates, so the highest sequence for a key always wins, even when updates arrive out of order. REPLACE USING doesn't require a change data capture feed with explicit insert, update, and delete operations, and it doesn't require a primary key.

See Apply partial snapshot replacement with REPLACE USING flows.

articles.summary:

articles.title: Databricks Runtime 19: August 10, 2026
articles.summary:
New features and improvements

  • collect_union aggregate function: SQL and the Scala and Python DataFrame APIs now support collect_union, which returns the distinct union of the elements in arrays within each group.

Behavioral changes

  • HAVING is evaluated before window functions in queries with generators: For queries that include generators, such as explode, window functions are now evaluated after the HAVING filter. Window results therefore include only rows retained by HAVING.
  • DataFrame.observe reports metrics from the last successful attempt: When a stage backing an observed operator is recomputed, observed metrics now reflect only the last successful attempt instead of combining values from multiple attempts.
  • Policy logic is hidden in query plans by default: Query plans no longer expose row filter and column mask policy logic unless the user has the INSPECT_POLICY_EXECUTION metastore privilege.
  • CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW preserves metadata atomically: For Unity Catalog views, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW now performs an atomic replacement that preserves the view identity, grants, tags, and comments by default. Governed tag protections continue to apply.
  • Delta API DML uses policy-definer rights: DeltaTable.delete, DeltaTable.update, and DeltaTable.merge now resolve row filter and column mask policy functions with the policy definer's rights, matching SQL DML. Callers no longer need EXECUTE on those policy functions when they have the required table permissions.

Library and environment updates

  • Updated Java from Zulu21.48+15-CA to Zulu21.50+19-CA.

articles.title: READ METADATA privilege is GA
articles.summary:
The READ METADATA privilege is now generally available in Unity Catalog.

READ METADATA provides read-only visibility into the same metadata available to the object's owner or a user with MANAGE, including security-sensitive information that BROWSE doesn't expose, such as privilege grants, row filters and column masks, and ABAC policies. It's intended for users who inspect and debug access controls, such as security auditors, data governance teams, and SREs.

You can grant READ METADATA on a range of object types. For the full list of applicable object types, see READ METADATA.

See READ METADATA.

articles.title: Notion connector (Beta)
articles.summary: The managed Notion connector in Lakeflow Connect is now available in Beta. The connector ingests pages, data sources, databases, blocks, comments, and users from Notion into Databricks. See Notion connector.

articles.summary:

articles.title: Orchestrate continuous pipelines with continuous jobs
articles.summary:
You can now run a continuous Lakeflow pipeline with a continuous job. When a continuous job orchestrates a pipeline, the job determines the execution mode, and the pipeline can use job-level features such as serverless Standard performance mode and additional notification destinations. Databricks recommends this pattern over the pipeline's built-in continuous setting, which is not being removed.

See Run a continuous pipeline with a continuous job and Run a pipeline continuously with a continuous job.

articles.title: Alert system tables are in Public Preview
articles.summary:
The system.alert schema is in Public Preview. This schema contains the alerts table, which records the configuration of every alert, and the alert_evaluation_history table, which records one row per alert evaluation. Use these tables to audit alert definitions, analyze evaluation trends, and monitor alert workloads at scale.

See Alert system tables reference.

articles.title: Tag automations (Beta)
articles.summary:
Tag automations are now in Beta. A tag automation assigns or removes governed tags on the Unity Catalog tables or volumes that match conditions you define, so tags stay accurate as your data and metadata change. Use them to certify trusted data, deprecate stale data, roll up column sensitivity to a table-level tier, flag assets that are missing required tags, and clean up outdated tags.

You can build an automation by describing your rule to Genie in natural language, or by filling in the scope, conditions, and action yourself. Saving an automation starts a dry run, which records the assets it would match without assigning any tags.

See Automate tag assignment.

articles.title: Change data feed on materialized views (Beta)
articles.summary:
You can now read a change data feed from a materialized view created in a Lakeflow pipeline or in Databricks SQL, using Databricks Runtime 18 LTS or above. Use this to replicate materialized view changes to destinations outside Databricks, or to keep a history of materialized view changes for auditing and reporting. Materialized views use automatic change data feed, so the change data feed is available for any materialized view with row tracking enabled, without configuring each materialized view. This feature is in Beta.

See Read a change data feed from a materialized view.

articles.title: ai_search function (Beta)
articles.summary:
The ai_search() SQL function retrieves information from one or more AI Search indexes configured as knowledge sources. Given a natural-language query, the function generates optimized search queries, retrieves and deduplicates results across sources, reranks them by relevance, and returns the most relevant documents. By default, it also synthesizes a grounded natural-language answer over those documents.

Use ai_search to enrich operational data with relevant context at scale, build batch retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, or expose retrieval as a tool to a compound AI system. This feature is in Beta.

See ai_search function.

articles.title: JAR tasks on serverless compute are now generally available
articles.summary: Package Scala or Java code as a JAR and run it as a task in a Lakeflow Job on serverless compute. Your JAR must match the Scala, Java Development Kit (JDK), and Databricks Connect versions of your serverless environment version. See Create and run JARs on serverless compute.

articles.title: Databricks-managed MCP connectors are now integrated with Unity Gateway (Beta)

Users must reauthenticate their connectors to continue using them with Genie One and Genie Code. A notification in Genie prompts impacted users to reconnect.

See the Unity Gateway API reference.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes

Click a widget's title or description to open a formatting toolbar, where you can apply text styling, links, and tables, or enter Markdown text directly. See Format widget titles and descriptions.
  • Hide pivot table column headers: Dashboard authors can now hide the column header in a pivot table. See Value-level settings.
  • Schedule run history: Dashboard authors can now see the run history for a schedule, including the run ID, start and end times, and status for each of the five most recent runs. See View schedule run history.
  • Pivot table grand totals fix: Fixed a bug where grand totals and expand and collapse controls did not appear on pivot tables.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Markdown tables in Agent mode APIs (Beta): In the Agent mode APIs, table visualizations now return as markdown instead of table visualization attachments, which improves readability. See the Agent mode API reference.
  • Longer agent descriptions: Genie Agents now show more of an agent's description by default, so you can see the purpose of each agent at a glance.
  • Comment on answers from Genie One: You can now add text comments to Genie Agent answers from Genie One.
  • Conversation mode in list APIs: The list conversations APIs now include a field that indicates whether a conversation was sent in Agent mode or Chat mode.
  • Download CSV in embedded agents: In embedded Genie Agents, download CSV actions now run inside the iframe instead of sending you to a separate page.
  • Agent thumbnail fix: Fixed a bug where Genie Agent thumbnails appeared too small in Genie One.
  • Agent mode benchmark results fix: Fixed a bug where agent mode benchmark results appeared as chat mode results.
  • Benchmark error messages: Benchmark runs now show a descriptive error message when a transient issue interrupts a run. Previously, these runs returned empty results with no explanation.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Upload PDF files to a conversation (Beta): You can now upload PDF files to a Genie One conversation alongside CSV and Excel files. Genie One parses PDFs asynchronously. See Upload a file.
  • Mention workspace users in document comments: In a document, you can now mention workspace users in a comment.
  • Genie Ontology enabled by default (Public Preview): The ontology is a unified context layer that gives Genie a business-aware map of your organization. It is now enabled by default. See Genie Ontology.

articles.title: Zerobus Ingest is now enabled by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile
articles.summary: The Zerobus Ingest connector in Lakeflow Connect is now enabled by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. See Zerobus Ingest overview.

articles.title: REPLACE USING flows for pipelines (Beta)
articles.summary:
REPLACE USING flows are now available in Lakeflow pipelines in Beta.

Use a REPLACE USING flow when your source is a series of partial snapshots keyed by column. On each update, the flow replaces all rows that match the specified key columns and leaves all other rows unchanged. A SEQUENCE BY column orders the updates, so the highest sequence for a key always wins, even when updates arrive out of order. REPLACE USING doesn't require a change data capture feed with explicit insert, update, and delete operations, and it doesn't require a primary key.

See Partial snapshot replacement with REPLACE USING flows.
