articles.title: MANAGE no longer requires USE CATALOG or USE SCHEMA on the same object
articles.summary:
The MANAGE privilege no longer requires a usage privilege (USE CATALOG or USE SCHEMA) on the object where MANAGE is granted. This change makes MANAGE behave more consistently with object ownership.

Previously, MANAGE on a catalog or schema took effect only if you also held the appropriate usage privileges on that object. You still need usage privileges on any parent containers:

  • MANAGE on a catalog requires no usage privileges.
  • MANAGE on a schema requires USE CATALOG on the parent catalog, but no longer requires USE SCHEMA on the schema.
  • MANAGE on a table, view, volume, or function is unchanged. It still requires USE CATALOG on the parent catalog and USE SCHEMA on the parent schema.

All other privileges are unaffected and still require usage privileges as prerequisites, even for users with MANAGE. For example, querying a table still requires SELECT on the table, plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on the parent catalog and schema.

If you granted MANAGE broadly without also granting the corresponding usage privileges, those grants are now active, and holders can manage the object. Databricks recommends auditing existing MANAGE grants to confirm they reflect your intended access.

See Usage privilege requirements for MANAGE.

articles.title: Refresh materialized views and streaming tables without exempting the pipeline owner from ABAC policies
articles.summary:
You can now refresh a pipeline-managed materialized view or streaming table even when the pipeline owner or run-as identity is subject to an attribute-based access control (ABAC) policy.

Previously, refreshing a materialized view or streaming table managed by a pipeline required the pipeline owner or run-as identity to be exempt from any applicable ABAC policy. That limitation has been removed.

When a pipeline refreshes a materialized view or streaming table, policies are evaluated using the pipeline owner's or run-as identity. If you don't want the persisted data to be masked or filtered, add the pipeline owner or run-as identity to the EXCEPT clause of ABAC policies associated with all the tables being read during the pipeline refresh. Use the TO clause to specify which users and groups receive masked or filtered data.

See ABAC policies on materialized views and streaming tables.

See Claude Max and Anthropic Enterprise support.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Dashboard relationships from imported BI files: When you import a Power BI or Tableau file with Genie Code, migration tooling now creates dashboard relationships where it detects them in the source file. See Import BI files using Genie Code.

  • Customize date picker quick-select options with Genie Code: You can now ask Genie Code for dashboard authoring to customize the quick-select options in a date range picker filter, such as keeping only day-based ranges. For an example prompt, see Optional: Customize the date picker quick-select options with Genie Code.

  • Full undo and redo in Genie Code: Genie Code for dashboard authoring now supports full undo and redo. Each Genie Code response is a single step that you can undo as a unit, including restoring an emptied dashboard. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.

  • Semantic validation for AI-authored metrics: Genie Code for dashboard authoring now automatically runs a semantic validation check after it creates a widget. The check validates business definitions, grain, attribution, population, time window, units, scale, and category values to improve the accuracy and consistency of metrics.

  • Low-code filters on measures: Local metric views now provide a low-code option for adding filters to measures. See Step 3: Define a filter.

  • Improved low-code UI for imported metric views: Metric views imported from Unity Catalog now use an improved low-code UI for extensions and modifications. See Extend a Unity Catalog metric view.

  • Metric view display names on dashboard widgets: Dashboard widgets now show the display name defined for each field in a local metric view instead of the literal field name. See Local metric views.

  • Cross-filtering includes the facet field: Cross-filtering on a faceted chart now includes the facet field as part of the filter. See Apply cross-filtering.

  • Applied filters in email attachments: Dashboard authors can now include the applied filters as a separate tabular attachment in email subscriptions. See Data attachments.

  • Warehouse picker for full-page Genie Code: The warehouse picker now appears for full-page Genie Code. See Full page Genie Code.

  • Dark mode scrollbar fix: Fixed a bug where the filter drop-down scrollbar did not appear in dark mode.

  • Line chart tooltip fix: Fixed a bug where tooltips did not appear on line charts.

articles.title: Upcoming general availability of Unity Gateway
articles.summary:
Unity Gateway, the Databricks governance solution for enterprise AI, is scheduled for general availability soon. Built on Unity Catalog, Unity Gateway extends governance to the runtime interactions between models, agents, MCP servers, and tools. You can control which AI services teams use, route and manage AI traffic, and monitor usage from one control plane.

The following capabilities will be generally available. Model, MCP, and model provider services are Unity Catalog securables that you govern with the same privileges as tables and volumes:

  • Model services route requests to pay-per-token and external models with traffic splitting and fallback, and you can share them across workspaces. See Custom model services.
  • MCP services register external or Databricks-provided MCP servers, so you can govern agent access with grants and tool selection. See MCPs.
  • Model provider services represent external model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon Bedrock, with centrally managed credentials. See Model providers external to Databricks.
  • Budgets monitor and control monthly Unity Gateway spend with per-user thresholds and hard caps. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway.

Unity Gateway will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in mid-September 2026.

See AI governance with Unity Gateway.

Automatic upgrades turn on a feature only after the observation window verifies that every client accessing a table supports it. To track which features are available for automatic upgrades, see Supported features.

articles.title: Python UDTFs in Unity Catalog are now generally available
articles.summary:
Registering Python user-defined table functions (UDTFs) in Unity Catalog is now generally available in Databricks Runtime 18. A Unity Catalog Python UDTF is a governed function that returns a table, invoked in the FROM clause of a SQL statement to return multiple rows and columns. Unity Catalog Python UDTFs run on serverless compute, classic compute with standard access mode, and SQL warehouses.

See Python user-defined table functions (UDTFs) in Unity Catalog and Databricks Runtime 18 LTS.

Test edge cases and iterate using mock inputs for supported table-identifier operations; review the isolation limitations before running tests. This feature is in Beta.

See Unit testing for pipelines.

You can assign a compute resource to a group using the Dedicated access mode, letting group members share compute while securely running languages and workloads not supported by standard access mode, such as Databricks Runtime for ML, RDD APIs, and R. When a user connects to a group cluster, their permissions down-scope to the group's permissions for the cluster session.

articles.title: Lakeflow Designer Summer Release
articles.summary:
The Lakeflow Designer Summer Release adds new operators, expands the Output and Join operators, and improves the canvas editing experience. The following updates are now available:

  • Prepare operator: Use the new Prepare operator for common data-cleansing tasks, including changing text case and data types, replacing values, and applying formulas. See Prepare.
  • Enter Data operator: Manually create tabular data in a spreadsheet-style editor. See Enter Data.
  • Select operator: Use the new Select operator to choose which columns to keep, rename columns, and reorder them in the output. See Select.
  • Visualization operator: Create and view visualizations directly on the canvas. See Visualization.
  • Improved Output operator: The Output operator now supports inserting or appending data in Unity Catalog tables, publishing results as materialized views, and writing CSV, Excel, or JSON files to Unity Catalog volumes. See Output.
  • Split Join outputs: The Join operator now provides three outputs by default: unmatched left rows, matched rows, and unmatched right rows. This makes it easier to branch a workflow based on join results. See Join.
  • Case-sensitive joins: The Join operator now includes a Match case option and matches string keys case-insensitively by default.
  • Matched and unmatched Filter outputs: The Filter operator now provides separate outputs for matching and non-matching rows, so you can branch data based on whether it meets the filter conditions. See Filter.
  • Improved date filtering: The Filter operator's date picker now supports navigating across years as well as months.
  • Additional AI functions: The AI Function operator now supports ai_query, ai_parse_document, ai_forecast, and ai_prep_search. See AI Function.
  • Folder and volume inputs: The Source operator can now target an entire Unity Catalog volume or folder path instead of an individual file. See Source.
  • Metric view sources: Use Unity Catalog metric views as source nodes in Lakeflow Designer. See Source.
  • Inline Note editing: The Note operator now supports inline rich-text editing directly on the canvas, including headings, text styling, links, images, and tables. See Note.
  • Easier node connections: Redesigned node ports provide larger connection targets and clearer visual cues, making operators easier to connect.
  • Clearer operator configuration cues: Unconfigured operators now have a dashed border, and required input ports that aren't connected are highlighted in yellow.
  • Table of contents panel: Find and navigate to any operator using the new searchable table of contents in the left sidebar. Select an operator to focus it on the canvas, then expand the Generated code section to view its underlying code.
  • Command palette: Press Cmd+Shift+P on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows to quickly access editor actions.
  • Visual data prep listing page: Find all of your visual data prep files from a dedicated Visual data prep page in the sidebar. The page includes a getting-started video banner to help you start using Lakeflow Designer.
  • Improved caching: On all-purpose compute, downstream operators can reuse cached upstream results, reducing repeated work for long-running steps such as AI functions.
  • Large-canvas performance: Scrolling and panning are more responsive on canvases with more than 200 operators.
  • Serverless environment selection: When working with visual data prep files, you can now choose the serverless environment used for both interactive runs and scheduled jobs.
  • Improved scheduled-job readability: Scheduled visual data prep runs now display each operator as an individual node in the Jobs task graph instead of showing raw Python code.
  • Declarative Automation Bundles support: Deploy and run visual data prep files with Declarative Automation Bundles by configuring them as notebook tasks and referencing the file path in notebook_task.notebook_path. See Move a visual data prep file to production.

articles.title: Databricks Runtime 19: July 23, 2026
articles.summary:
Databricks Runtime 19 is now generally available (GA). For lifecycle details, see Databricks Runtime support lifecycles.

Behavioral changes

  • Arrow-optimized Python UDFs enabled by default: Regular Python UDFs now use Arrow-based serialization by default. This can change type-coercion behavior for some UDFs compared to previous releases. To restore the previous behavior, set spark.databricks.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled to false.

New features and improvements

  • TopN pushdown for fine-grained access control on dedicated compute: Fine-grained access control on dedicated compute now pushes down ORDER BY ... LIMIT (TopN) operations to the remote cluster that performs the filtering, improving query performance.
  • parquet-java upgraded to 1.17.0: The apache/parquet-java dependency is upgraded to version 1.17.0. For the full list of changes, see the apache/parquet-java release notes.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Higher character limit for uploaded PDFs: The maximum number of characters per uploaded PDF has been raised from 4,000 to 15,000. See PDF files.
  • Agent mode APIs (Beta): Agent mode APIs for Genie Agents are now available in Beta. See the Agent mode API reference.
  • Analyze files in Unity Catalog volumes (Beta): A Genie Agent can now analyze files stored in Unity Catalog volumes, such as PDFs, slide decks, and images. See Attach volumes to a Genie Agent.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Import BI files (Public Preview): Importing Power BI and Tableau reports as AI/BI dashboards with Genie Code is in Public Preview. See Import BI files using Genie Code.

  • Image widget: You can now add a dedicated image widget to a dashboard. See Image widgets.

  • Multi-select filter improvements: Multi-select filter improvements:

    • Multi-select filter stays open: Multi-select filter drop-downs now stay open between selections and keep your place in the list instead of closing.
    • Select all matching values in a multi-select filter: In a multi-select filter, you can now type to narrow the list and select Select all results to select every matching value at once. Selections are additive across searches.

  • Dashboard variable display names: When a display name is available, dashboard variable drop-down menu options show the column's display name instead of the field name. To learn more about variables, see Create a dashboard variable.

  • Cross-filtering text-selection fix: Fixed a bug where selecting text in a table unintentionally triggered cross-filtering.

  • Dark mode filter dropdown scrollbar fix: Fixed a bug where the scrollbar in dashboard filter dropdowns wasn't visible in dark mode.

  • Genie Code for dashboard authoring: Genie Code for dashboard authoring, the Genie agent built for authoring dashboards, is now generally available. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring. This release also adds the following authoring capabilities:

    • Author image widgets with Genie Code: Genie Code for dashboard authoring can now add image widgets to a dashboard. See Author image widgets.
    • Beautify dashboards with Genie Code: Genie Code for dashboard authoring can now redesign a dashboard's appearance. Ask it to beautify your dashboard, then undo the changes if you want to revert. See Beautify a dashboard.

articles.title: Variant will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Variant will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in July 2026.

Use Variant to ingest semi-structured data from streaming sources (Kinesis, Event Hub), REST APIs, and schemaless databases, while maintaining high-performance query access.

See Variant type support for Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake.

articles.title: Variant and Variant shredding are now generally available
articles.summary:
Variant is now generally available. Variant is a flexible data type for semi-structured data that delivers structured-like query performance through Variant shredding, which is also generally available. Use Variant to ingest semi-structured data from streaming sources (Kinesis, Event Hub), REST APIs, and schemaless databases, while maintaining high-performance query access.

Starting with Databricks Runtime 17.3, Variant shredding is automatically enabled when you create a new table with VARIANT columns. For optimal query performance with variant statistics collection and data skipping, Databricks recommends Databricks Runtime 18.1 or above. See Use variant shredding to optimize performance.

Variant is coming soon to workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

articles.title: Transactions are now generally available
articles.summary:
Transactions that write to Unity Catalog managed Delta tables are now generally available. Group multiple SQL statements across one or more tables into a single atomic transaction using BEGIN ATOMIC ... END; or BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... COMMIT; syntax. All changes succeed together or roll back together, ensuring data consistency across your operations. Transactions require catalog commits enabled on participating tables. Transactions that write to Unity Catalog managed Iceberg tables remain in Private Preview.

See Transactions.

articles.title: Email notifications for expiring service principal tokens are now generally available
articles.summary:
Databricks now automatically sends an email notification when a service principal token is set to expire within seven days. Because service principals don't have their own mailboxes, Databricks sends these notifications to workspace admins. Notifications are sent only for service principal tokens that have a lifetime longer than seven days and have been used at least once. No configuration is required.

See Service principal token expiration notifications.

articles.title: Databricks-hosted sample datasets available in the samples catalog
articles.summary:
The sample datasets /databricks-datasets mounted to DBFS are now also available in the samples catalog as samples.databricks.datasets, made available through OpenSharing. The datasets volume hosts a collection of Databricks-provided datasets that you can use to build and test data pipelines.

The samples catalog is available in Unity Catalog-enabled workspaces. For more information about the sample datasets available in the samples catalog, see Sample datasets.

articles.title: Override the REPLACE WHERE predicate for a single refresh
articles.summary: You can now override a standalone streaming table's defined REPLACE WHERE predicate for a single refresh by adding a WHERE clause to the REFRESH STREAMING TABLE command. The override applies only to that refresh and doesn't change the table definition, which is useful for one-time backfills and corrections. This is supported only on standalone streaming tables created with a FLOW REPLACE WHERE clause. See REFRESH (MATERIALIZED VIEW or STREAMING TABLE).

articles.title: Role-based access control (RBAC) is in Public Preview
articles.summary:
Role-based access control (RBAC) is now in Public Preview. RBAC lets users assume a role in Databricks using only that role's permissions for the duration of the session instead of their own accumulated permissions. This enables exclusive access. Users must actively assume a role to reach sensitive data, which prevents them from accessing it as their own identity and from mixing data across use cases, clinical trials, projects, or clients.

To enable RBAC, an account admin turns on the preview at the account level. Workspace admins then enable it in each workspace.

See Role-based access control (RBAC).

articles.title: Lakeflow Designer support for compliance security profile standards
articles.summary:
Lakeflow Designer now supports all compliance security profile standards supported by Databricks and is available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

For a full list of supported compliance standards, see Compliance security profile.

See Lakeflow Designer.

articles.title: Governance Hub is in Beta
articles.summary:
Governance Hub is in Beta. Governance Hub is a centralized, account-level UI in the account console for monitoring governance across your Databricks account. It provides a unified view of data health and coverage, AI usage and spend, and cost drivers, with prioritized insights and recommendations. All views respect existing permissions.

Account admins can enable Governance Hub from the account console Previews page. See Governance Hub.

articles.title: Priority pay-per-token for Foundation Model APIs
articles.summary:
Priority pay-per-token, also referred to as priority mode, for Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token is generally available for partner models and in preview for open source models.

Priority mode is for latency-sensitive, real-time applications that need more consistent availability under load.

See Priority pay-per-token for Foundation Model APIs for model availability.

articles.title: Automated setup for S3 external locations
articles.summary: You can now create an S3 external location using automated setup, the recommended method for connecting an S3 bucket to Databricks. Automated setup uses AWS IAM temporary delegation to configure your external location and provision all required resources, including the IAM role, storage credential, and external location. It also provides built-in approval workflows for users who need AWS admin authorization. See Create an external location with automated setup.

articles.title: Warehouse-level statement timeouts (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now set a statement timeout on a single SQL warehouse so that different warehouses can apply different timeouts to their queries. Set the timeout with the statement_timeout field in the Create or Update warehouse APIs. This feature is in Beta and is API-only. See Warehouse-level timeout.

articles.title: Reddit Ads connector is now available in Beta
articles.summary: The managed Reddit Ads connector in Lakeflow Connect is now available in Beta. You can use the connector to ingest advertising campaign data and performance metrics from Reddit Ads into Databricks. See Reddit Ads connector.

articles.title: Genie One and Genie Agents billed usage corrections
articles.summary:
Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free through January 31, 2027.

Beginning July 21, 2026, Databricks is applying a correction so that Genie One and Genie Agents usage is properly reflected as free across your billing data and budgets:

  • System tables: Correction records land in system.billing.usage that negate prior Genie One and Genie Agents billed usage, so that aggregated billable usage is zero. See Record type reference and Monitor and understand your Genie cost.
  • Budgets: Genie One and Genie Agents costs are netted out of budget enforcement. As a result, spend shown in the budget UI will drop slightly. In some cases, a user who was previously over their budget threshold may fall back under it once their Genie One and Genie Agents costs are netted out.

This is a one-time adjustment. Genie Code usage and billing are unaffected.

articles.title: Google Gemini 3.6 Flash now available as a Databricks-hosted model
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports Google Gemini 3.6 Flash as a Databricks-hosted model. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite now available as a Databricks-hosted model
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports Google Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite as a Databricks-hosted model. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Context-based ingress control for workspaces public access is now generally available
articles.summary: Context-based ingress control for workspaces public access is now generally available. Control who can reach your workspace endpoints using allow and deny rules that allow you to combine identities, network sources, and request types. See Context-based ingress control.

articles.title: Genie One and Genie Agents billed usage corrections
articles.summary:
Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free through January 31, 2027.

Beginning July 21, 2026, Databricks is applying a correction so that Genie One and Genie Agents usage is properly reflected as free across your billing data and budgets:

  • System tables: Correction records land in system.billing.usage that negate prior Genie One and Genie Agents billed usage, so that aggregated billable usage is zero. See Record type reference and Monitor and understand your Genie cost.
  • Budgets: Genie One and Genie Agents costs are netted out of budget enforcement. As a result, spend shown in the budget UI will drop slightly. In some cases, a user who was previously over their budget threshold may fall back under it once their Genie One and Genie Agents costs are netted out.

This is a one-time adjustment. Genie Code usage and billing are unaffected.

articles.title: Mention Genie Code in notebook comments
articles.summary: You can now mention Genie Code in a notebook comment to get AI help without leaving the comment thread. Type @ in a comment, select Genie Code, and enter your request. Genie Code replies inline in the thread. See Code comments.

articles.title: Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams is now in Public Preview
articles.summary: The Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams is now in Public Preview. The app brings Genie into Microsoft Teams so users can ask data questions and get answers without leaving Microsoft Teams. See Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams.

articles.title: Connect and govern any external model provider
articles.summary:
Connect and govern any external model provider (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, and newly released models like Meta's Muse Spark 1.1) through Unity Gateway. Register a provider once as a governed Unity Catalog securable, and every team can query it through Unity Gateway with full governance and observability.

With external model providers, you get:

  • Choice: Adopt any model on day one, and switch between models or OpenAI-compatible providers without re-integrating.
  • Control: Govern access with standard GRANT and REVOKE (EXECUTE to query, MANAGE to update), and attach rate limits and guardrails that apply to every request.
  • Clarity: Usage and spend tracking is on by default, with token counts, latency, and cost attribution per user, team, or app. Attach inference tables to log full request and response payloads to a governed Delta table.

See Model providers external to Databricks.

articles.title: Anthropic managed ingestion connector (Beta)
articles.summary: The Anthropic connector in Lakeflow Connect is now available in Beta. The connector allows you to ingest Compliance API data — audit activity, organizations, users, roles, groups, settings, and Claude chats and messages — from Anthropic into Databricks. See Anthropic connector.

articles.title: Connect and govern any external model provider
articles.summary:
Connect and govern any external model provider (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, and newly released models like Meta's Muse Spark 1.1) through Unity Gateway. Register a provider once as a governed Unity Catalog securable, and every team can query it through Unity Gateway with full governance and observability.

With external model providers, you get:

  • Choice: Adopt any model on day one, and switch between models or OpenAI-compatible providers without re-integrating.
  • Control: Govern access with standard GRANT and REVOKE (EXECUTE to query, MANAGE to update), and attach rate limits and guardrails that apply to every request.
  • Clarity: Usage and spend tracking is on by default, with token counts, latency, and cost attribution per user, team, or app. Attach inference tables to log full request and response payloads to a governed Delta table.

See Model providers external to Databricks.

articles.title: MLflow trace storage in Unity Catalog will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
MLflow trace storage in Unity Catalog tables will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in mid-August 2026.

Store MLflow traces in Unity Catalog tables for scalable, governed trace storage: storage is unlimited, traces are stored in OpenTelemetry (OTel) format, access is governed through Unity Catalog schema and table permissions, and you can query traces with SQL. To view traces, point an MLflow experiment at a Unity Catalog trace location.

See Store OpenTelemetry traces in Unity Catalog.

articles.title: Scala and Java UDFs in Unity Catalog are now generally available
articles.summary:
Register Scala and Java user-defined functions (UDFs) in Unity Catalog and reuse them across notebooks, jobs, and SQL warehouses with Unity Catalog governance. Reuse existing JVM logic and get better performance than Python UDFs on all compute, including serverless.

See Scala and Java user-defined functions (UDFs) in Unity Catalog.

For workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled, see What's coming for planned availability changes.

articles.title: MLflow trace storage in Unity Catalog is now generally available
articles.summary:
MLflow trace storage in Unity Catalog tables is now generally available. Databricks recommends storing traces in Unity Catalog for new and production workloads: storage is unlimited, traces are stored in OpenTelemetry (OTel) format, access is governed through Unity Catalog schema and table permissions, and you can query traces with SQL, Genie, AI/BI dashboards, and any Spark-based tool. To view traces, point an MLflow experiment at a Unity Catalog trace location. For supported regions, see Features with limited regional availability.

See Store OpenTelemetry traces in Unity Catalog and Observe and find issues.

articles.title: Agentic code converter is in Beta
articles.summary:
The agentic code converter is in Beta. Use it to convert legacy SQL dialects, such as T-SQL, Snowflake, Redshift, Oracle, BigQuery, and Teradata, to ANSI SQL in migration projects in your workspace. Powered by Genie Code, the converter analyzes each source script, validates syntax and semantic intent, and iteratively fixes errors before writing the results to your workspace. A workspace admin must enable it from the Previews page.

See Convert SQL with the agentic code converter.

articles.title: Google Gemini 3 Pro is retired
articles.summary: Google Gemini 3 Pro is retired. Gemini 3.1 Pro is the recommended replacement. See Deprecated and retired models for migration guidance.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Search and reuse past conversations: You can now search your past Genie One conversations and bring previous context into your current conversation. See Recall past conversations.
  • Memory (Beta): Genie One can remember details you ask it to save, such as your preferences and workflows, and applies them in future conversations. See Add to Genie One's memory.
  • Mention scheduled tasks: You can now @mention scheduled tasks in Genie One. See Scheduled tasks.
  • New chat loading fix: Fixed a bug where a new chat showed a blank screen while waiting for the first response.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Save a chat as a Genie Agent: You can now save a Genie One thread as a Genie Agent. See Create an agent.
  • Conversation sharing (Public Preview): Sharing an individual Genie Agent conversation is now in Public Preview. See Share a conversation.
  • Access email terminology: Access-granted and access-request emails now use the Genie Agent's name.
  • Download visualization fix: Fixed a bug where choropleth and point map visualizations were not returned by the download visualization API.
  • Benchmark results fix: Fixed a bug where benchmark results incorrectly showed as empty.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Git folders: Git folders for dashboards are now generally available. See Version control dashboards with Git.
  • Run a schedule on demand: You can now select Run now on a dashboard schedule to run it immediately. See Manage schedules.
  • Improved Ask Genie starter questions: Ask Genie suggests better starter questions for dashboards and caches them to reduce latency.
  • Genie Code error handling: When you author a dashboard with Genie Code, it now returns an error instead of retrying SQL queries that are not valid. This behavior reduces the cost of query errors.
  • Bookmark icon visibility: When viewing a published dashboard, the bookmark icon no longer appears if a dashboard has no bookmarks.
  • Ask Genie health-check fix: Ask Genie no longer shows a health-check warning when the linked Genie Agent is still usable.
  • Dashboard creation fix: Fixed a bug where some authors with the SQL access entitlement could not create or clone dashboards.
  • PNG download fix: Fixed a bug where custom fonts were dropped from the chart title and legend in single-widget PNG downloads.
  • Waterfall chart fix: Fixed a bug where y-axis formatting options on a waterfall chart did not work.

articles.title: AI Search high QPS will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
AI Search high QPS will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled in late August 2026.

Set a target QPS on standard AI Search endpoints to power high-throughput, real-time workloads like search bars, recommendation systems, and entity matching. High QPS is enabled by default, but existing endpoints are not affected. Additional capacity and the associated cost apply only when you configure a target QPS for an endpoint.

See Scale AI Search endpoint throughput with high QPS.

articles.title: Lakebase now provides a service level agreement (SLA)
articles.summary: Lakebase now provides a Service Level Agreement (SLA), with Monthly Uptime Percentage commitments for endpoints in zone-redundant high availability mode and for single-compute endpoints. For details, see Lakebase SLA.

articles.title: Thinking Machine Labs Inkling now available as a Databricks-hosted model in Public Preview
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports Thinking Machine Labs Inkling as a Databricks-hosted model. This mixture of experts (MoE) model supports text and image inputs, a 1 million token context window, and is optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic tool-use tasks. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Inkling is available in Public Preview.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free through January 31, 2027
articles.summary:
As of July 15, 2026, billing for Genie One and Genie Agents is paused, and usage of these products is free through January 31, 2027. Budget controls do not apply to them.

Genie Code continues to be billed under the pay-as-you-go pricing model. For more information about pricing, see Databricks pricing.

articles.title: Data Classification is now available by default for additional compliance standards
articles.summary: Data Classification is now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled and either C5, TISAX, or IRAP controls selected.

articles.title: Custom URLs for your Databricks account (Public Preview)
articles.summary: You can now claim and enable a Custom URL that gives your Databricks account a single, branded entry point (for example, acme.databricks.com) for all users and workspaces. See Give your Databricks account a custom URL.

articles.title: AI Search High QPS is now generally available
articles.summary:
AI Search High QPS is now generally available for standard endpoints.

Set a target QPS on standard AI Search endpoints to power high-throughput, real-time workloads like search bars, recommendation systems, and entity matching. High QPS is enabled by default, but existing endpoints are not affected. Additional capacity and the associated cost apply only when you configure a target QPS for an endpoint.

See Scale AI Search endpoint throughput with high QPS.

articles.title: ai_extract and ai_classify are now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
The ai_extract and ai_classify SQL AI functions are now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled and HIPAA, PCI-DSS, FedRAMP Moderate, CCCS Medium (Protected B), UK Cyber Essentials Plus, HITRUST, IRAP, C5, and TISAX controls selected.

Use ai_extract to extract structured fields from unstructured text against a user-defined schema. Use ai_classify to classify text into user-defined labels for routing, tagging, and document categorization workflows. You can also use Agent Bricks to create an information extraction agent and a classification agent.

articles.title: Data Classification is now available by default for additional compliance standards
articles.summary: Data Classification is now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled and either C5, TISAX, or IRAP controls selected.

articles.title: Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free through January 31, 2027
articles.summary: Genie One and Genie Agents usage is free through January 31, 2027. Budget controls do not apply during this time.

articles.title: Query-based connectors in Lakeflow Connect will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Query-based connectors in Lakeflow Connect will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Query-based connectors ingest data from databases by querying the source directly using a cursor column, without requiring change data capture (CDC) configuration or an ingestion gateway. Supported sources include Oracle, Teradata, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL, as well as all Lakehouse Federation data sources using foreign catalog ingestion.

See Query-based connectors.

articles.title: Request for Access will soon be enabled by default for all workspaces
articles.summary:
In an upcoming release, Request for Access will be enabled by default for all workspaces, and access requests will be routed to the owner of the requested Unity Catalog object via email. You can configure access request destinations at any time in the metastore settings. The legacy workspace-level access request settings will be deprecated.

See Configure access request destinations for a metastore.

articles.title: Lakebase is now SOC 2 Type 2 compliant
articles.summary: Lakebase is now SOC 2 Type 2 compliant. For our SOC reports, please ask your Databricks account team or see Compliance.

articles.title: Allowlist partner platform IPs in context-based ingress control (Beta)
articles.summary: Context-based ingress control now supports Partner Platforms as a network source. Select a partner platform to allowlist the IPs that third-party apps use to connect to Databricks, including Power BI, Tableau Cloud, and dbt platform. Databricks manages and updates these IP lists automatically. See Network sources.

articles.title: Trigger.AvailableNow support for OpenSharing streaming (GA)
articles.summary:
Streaming reads from OpenSharing tables now support the Trigger.AvailableNow trigger. This trigger captures the shared table's current version when it starts, processes all available data across one or more micro-batches (honoring maxFilesPerTrigger and maxVersionsPerRpc), and then stops, which is well suited to scheduled, batch-like incremental processing. Previously, Trigger.AvailableNow on a OpenSharing source was converted to Trigger.Once, which processed a single micro-batch per run. This feature requires Databricks Runtime 18.0 or above.

See Query a table using Apache Spark Structured Streaming for Databricks-to-Databricks recipients and Access a shared table using Spark Structured Streaming for open sharing recipients.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.20 is rolling out in Current
articles.summary: Databricks SQL version 2026.20 is rolling out to the Current channel. See features in 2026.20.

articles.title: Automatic upgrades will roll out more features to existing tables
articles.summary:
Automatic upgrades apply recommended features to your Unity Catalog managed tables after verifying workload compatibility. Databricks is expanding the features that automatic upgrades apply to existing tables.

Starting in July 2026, automatic upgrades will roll out row tracking and Checkpoint V2 to existing tables. This rollout is gradual, so these features will be available to different customers at different times.

In August 2026, automatic upgrades will roll out catalog commits and deletion vectors to existing tables.

Automatic upgrades turn on a feature only after the observation window verifies that every client accessing a table supports it. To track which features are available for automatic upgrades, see Supported features.

articles.title: View warehouse activity details (General Availability)
articles.summary: The Activity details toggle in the SQL warehouse monitoring UI is now generally available. View color-coded annotations on the Running clusters chart that explain why a warehouse remains active, including query activity, fetching queries, open sessions, and idle states. Hover over bars to see metadata, or click on fetching activity to filter the query history table. See Activity details.

articles.title: Databricks-provided MCP Services will GA soon
articles.summary:
Databricks-provided MCP Services for SaaS applications such as Slack, GitHub, Atlassian, and Google Drive will soon be generally available, with both read and write operations enabled by default. Admins and users can disable MCP Services and individual tools in Unity Gateway.

See MCPs.

articles.title: Lakebase update notifications now post 3 days in advance
articles.summary:
To deliver Postgres version updates, security patches, and new features to your projects sooner, Lakebase has shortened the planned update notification window. Planned updates are now posted at least 3 days in advance, rather than 7. You can check your project's settings for upcoming updates.

See Manage updates.

articles.title: Secrets in Unity Catalog (Public Preview)
articles.summary: You can now store, govern, and access secrets as securable objects in Unity Catalog. A Unity Catalog secret uses the three-level namespace (catalog.schema.secret) and is governed by Unity Catalog privileges, so you can apply the same access controls and auditing that you use for other data assets. See Secrets in Unity Catalog.

articles.title: Change to default pipeline editor for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
The Lakeflow Pipelines Editor has been generally available since May 2026. In August, it will become the default editor for developing and debugging pipelines in workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. At that time the legacy editor will be removed.

For more information about the Lakeflow Pipelines Editor, see Develop and debug ETL pipelines with the Lakeflow Pipelines Editor. If you have questions about this transition, contact your account team.

articles.title: Strac connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Strac connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector ingests data-security audit events from your Strac instance into Databricks. Authentication uses a Strac API key.

See Strac connector.

articles.title: Protobuf tensor input for custom model serving endpoints (Public Preview)
articles.summary:
For custom model serving endpoints with a tensor-based input signature, you can now send the request body as a serialized KServe v2 ModelInferRequest with Content-Type: application/x-protobuf, instead of JSON.

This feature is in Public Preview and is only available on endpoints deployed after July 9, 2026. See Protobuf tensor input.

articles.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, and GPT-5.6 Luna now available as Databricks-hosted models
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, and GPT-5.6 Luna as Databricks-hosted models. You can access these models using Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Databricks SQL alerts are now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
articles.summary:
Databricks SQL alerts now support all compliance security profile standards that Databricks supports, and are available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

Use Databricks SQL alerts to monitor data and KPIs by running queries on a schedule, evaluating conditions, and notifying recipients when the conditions are met.

See Databricks SQL alerts.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Document citations: Documents now show citations that link content back to the data and sources Genie One used to generate the document. See View citations.

  • Document version history: Documents now keep a version history so you can review earlier versions. See View version history.

  • Open document links in soft tabs: Documents now support soft tabs, so you can open links without leaving the document. See Open links in soft tabs.

  • GitHub MCP (Beta): The GitHub MCP connection for Genie One is now in Beta. See GitHub.

  • Genie One MCP App (Beta): The Genie One MCP App adds rich UI interactions from third-party agents, including interactive visualizations and Genie Ontology citations. See Genie One MCP server.

  • Certified visualizations: SQL charts and visualizations that Genie One inserts are now read-only and appear as certified visuals.

articles.title: Front-end Private Link for account-level Genie One (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now configure front-end Private Link for account-level Genie One. Turn on the Front-end Private Link for Custom URLs and Account preview to get started. See Configure inbound Private Link for account-level resources.

articles.title: Genie Agents enhancements
articles.summary:
• Genie Agents (formerly Genie Spaces) renamed to Genie Agents: Genie Agents (formerly Genie Spaces) are now called Genie Agents.
  • SQL expressions grouped with example SQL: In the authoring experience, SQL expressions are now grouped with example SQL queries so you can define and manage both in one place. See Define SQL expressions.
  • Consistent Genie Agent experience in Genie One: In Genie One, a Genie Agent now opens as a chat if you have viewing rights only, or in the Analytics and AI workspace UI if you have authoring privileges. See Use Genie One.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Import BI files is in Public Preview: Importing Power BI and Tableau reports as AI/BI dashboards with Genie Code is in Public Preview. You can also start an import directly from the dashboard list page. See Import BI files using Genie Code.
  • Dashboard Ask Genie is generally available: The Ask Genie button on published dashboards is now generally available. See Genie Agents with dashboards.
  • Ask Genie handles partially supported datasets: When only some datasets in a dashboard use unsupported SQL expressions, Ask Genie now answers from the supported datasets instead of failing. See Incompatible SQL expressions.
  • English names for choropleth regions: Choropleth maps now support English region names from the name_en column as the identifier for admin-0 (country) boundaries. See Region.
  • Genie Code on by default for compliance security profile: For workspaces with a compliance security profile (CSP), Genie Code for dashboard authoring is now turned on by default and runs on Databricks-hosted models. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
  • Empty multi-select filter defaults in Genie Code: Genie Code can now use an empty multi-select (All) default for parameter filters instead of requiring a single default value.
  • Cluster-by and partition-by for local metric views: Local metric views now support cluster-by and partition-by configuration in the UI and YAML. See Local metric views.
  • Apply filters fix: Fixed a bug where the apply button on filters cleared the text input instead of applying the filter.
  • Dashboard import fix: Fixed a bug where importing a dashboard failed if it contained a bookmark that referenced a deleted widget.

articles.title: Behavior changes for continuous jobs and pipelines
articles.summary:
In early August 2026, continuous Lakeflow pipelines and jobs will receive updates to simplify configuration.

You will be able to configure a continuous schedule directly from the pipeline page, including job-level settings such as performance mode. Configuring a continuous schedule this way wraps the pipeline in a continuous job.

Databricks recommends running continuous pipelines with a continuous job rather than the pipeline's built-in continuous setting. When a continuous job wraps a pipeline, the job will manage the pipeline's execution lifecycle. The built-in continuous setting is not being removed, but new continuous pipelines should use the continuous job pattern.

articles.title: Object metadata column is now in Public Preview
articles.summary:
The _object_metadata column is now in Public Preview. The _object_metadata column is a hidden metadata column that exposes object-level properties for objects in cloud storage, including MIME type, ETag, user-defined key-value metadata, system-defined metadata, and object tags. It is available starting from Databricks Runtime 18.1.

See Object metadata column.

articles.title: Zhipu AI GLM 5.2 now available as a Databricks-hosted model
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports GLM 5.2 as a Databricks-hosted model. This mixture of experts (MoE) model supports a 1 million token context window and is optimized for long-horizon reasoning, coding, and agentic tool use. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Genie products now use pay-as-you-go pricing
articles.summary:
Starting July 8, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, Genie products, including Genie Agents, Genie Code, and Genie One, are billed following a pay-as-you-go pricing model that includes 150 Databricks units (DBUs) of free large language model (LLM) usage every month, equivalent to about $10.50 in the US East region. Usage beyond the free amount is billed in DBUs, reflecting the underlying LLM models and agents that power each Genie session. For more information about pricing, see Databricks pricing.

As of July 15, 2026, billing for Genie One and Genie Agents is paused, and usage of these products by users is free through January 31, 2027. Genie Code continues to be billed under this pay-as-you-go model.

To monitor and control Genie spend for your account, see Manage budgets and cost controls for Genie.

articles.title: Genie Spaces is now Genie Agents
articles.summary: Genie Spaces are now called Genie Agents. The name changed across the documentation, but the product's capabilities are unchanged. For more information, see Genie Agents.

articles.title: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro are scheduled for retirement
articles.summary: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash and Gemini 2.5 Pro will be retired on October 2, 2026. The recommended replacement models are Gemini 3.1 Pro or Gemini 3.5 Flash. See Deprecated and retired models for migration guidance.

articles.title: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4 is retired
articles.summary: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4 is retired as of October 9, 2026. Claude Sonnet 4.6 is the recommended replacement. See Deprecated and retired models for migration guidance.

articles.title: Restrict access to AI Functions with Unity Catalog permissions (Public Preview)
articles.summary: You can now use Unity Catalog permissions to restrict which task-specific AI Functions your organization can access, independent of foundation model access. Contact your account team to enable this feature. See AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions.

articles.title: Genie Agents now uses pay-as-you-go pricing
articles.summary:
Starting July 8, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, Genie Agents is billed following a pay-as-you-go pricing model that includes 150 DBUs of free large language model (LLM) usage every month, equivalent to about $10.50 in the US East region. Usage beyond the free amount is billed in DBUs, reflecting the underlying LLM models and agents that power each Genie Agents session. Account admins can set budgets to monitor and control Genie spend. See Manage budgets and cost controls for Genie and the Databricks pricing page.

As of July 15, 2026, billing for Genie One and Genie Agents is paused, and usage of these products by users is free through January 31, 2027. Genie Code continues to be billed under this pay-as-you-go model.

articles.title: REPLACE WHERE flows are now generally available
articles.summary: REPLACE WHERE flows for pipelines and standalone streaming tables are now generally available. Use them to replace only rows matching a predicate on each refresh, without reprocessing the full table history. See Batch processing with REPLACE WHERE flows.

articles.title: Managed Iceberg materialized views are in Public Preview
articles.summary: You can now create a materialized view that is compatible with external Iceberg readers. This feature is in Public Preview. To enable it, reach out to your Databricks account team. See Create a materialized view compatible with external Iceberg readers.

articles.title: Excel file format support is now available by default
articles.summary: Excel file format support is now available by default for all workspaces. You can ingest, parse, and query .xls, .xlsx, and .xlsm files directly using built-in support, without external libraries or manual conversions. See Read and stream Excel files.

articles.title: July 6, 2026
articles.summary:
This serverless compute release includes updates from Databricks Runtime 18.

New features

  • Spark Declarative Pipelines on Lakeflow streaming query ID: Spark Declarative Pipelines on Lakeflow can now set the streaming query ID on demand.

  • IP address functions (Public Preview): New SQL functions are available for working with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and CIDR blocks, including ip_host, ip_cidr, ip_version, ip_prefix_length, ip_network, ip_network_last, ip_cidr_contains, ip_as_binary, ip_as_string, and try_* variants for null-safe behavior. See ip_host and related functions.

  • On-demand state repartitioning (Public Preview): Structured Streaming now supports changing the number of shuffle partitions for stateful queries without losing checkpoint state. See On-demand state repartitioning for stateful streaming queries.

Behavior changes

  • CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE preserves comments: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE now preserves existing column and table comments by default. Previously, comments were dropped when recreating a table. Managed tables and views now match the existing behavior of materialized views and streaming tables.

  • DataFrame by-name writes cast compatible columns: writeTo().append(), writeTo().overwrite(), writeTo().overwritePartitions(), and write.mode("append").saveAsTable() now automatically cast type-compatible columns (for example, int to long) to match the target Delta table schema. Previously, these operations failed with a DELTA_FAILED_TO_MERGE_FIELDS error when column types were compatible but not identical. Behavior now matches SQL INSERT INTO ... BY NAME.

  • ALTER TABLE SET TBLPROPERTIES for pipelines.pipelineId: ALTER TABLE <table> SET TBLPROPERTIES('pipelines.pipelineId' = '<pipeline-id>') now attempts to make the specified table eligible for writes by the pipeline. Previously, setting this property on a regular table had no effect. If the table isn't eligible for pipeline writes, the command throws SETTING_PIPELINES_PIPELINE_ID_NOT_SUPPORTED.

  • DESCRIBE EXTENDED AS JSON includes predictive optimization results: DESCRIBE EXTENDED ... AS JSON now includes predictive optimization evaluation results in its output. Previously, this information wasn't returned in the JSON output.

  • Metric view window measures return correct results: Metric view window measures now return correct results when queries use GROUP BY, IN/BETWEEN filters, or mixed predicates on the window's order column. Previously, these filter patterns could produce incorrect results.

  • Structured Streaming deduplication with NaN keys: Structured Streaming deduplication now treats NaN (Not-a-Number) values that have different bit patterns as duplicates when a double or float column is used as a deduplication key. Previously, NaN values with different internal representations were treated as distinct and were not deduplicated.

  • NATURAL JOIN case-insensitive column matching: NATURAL JOIN now matches common columns case-insensitively, consistent with the equivalent USING join. Previously, column matching was case-sensitive, causing columns that differ only in case (for example, ID vs id) to not be recognized as common columns, resulting in a silent cross join instead of the expected equi-join.

articles.title: Standard performance mode is now supported for materialized view or streaming table refreshes in jobs
articles.summary:
Materialized view and streaming table refreshes that are orchestrated through a SQL task in a Lakeflow job now respect the job's Performance optimized setting. When the setting is turned off, the refresh uses standard performance mode, which consumes fewer DBUs.

For more about performance modes for scheduled refreshes, see Select a performance mode for scheduled refreshes.

articles.title: Budgets are now generally available
articles.summary:
Budgets, including budgets for Unity Gateway, are now generally available.

Budgets let admins define spending thresholds. For requests managed through Unity Gateway, including Genie interactions, admins can set additional per-user thresholds and overrides, with configurable actions such as email alerting and usage blocking.

See Create and monitor budgets and Manage budgets for Unity Gateway.

articles.title: Private Link for account-level resources (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now use Private Link to privately connect to Databricks account-level resources, such as the account console, through a VPC interface endpoint instead of the public internet. See Configure inbound Private Link for account-level resources.

articles.title: Okta support for automatic identity management is now generally available
articles.summary:
Okta support for automatic identity management is now generally available. Automatic identity management lets you sync users and groups from Okta into Databricks without SCIM provisioning. When enabled, you can search for users and groups directly in identity federated workspaces and add them to your workspace, and Databricks uses Okta as the source of record for group memberships.

See Configure Okta for automatic identity management.

articles.title: Lakeflow Connect row filtering is now generally available
articles.summary:
Row filtering in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available. Row filtering allows you to ingest only the rows you need by applying conditions similar to a SQL WHERE clause, improving performance and minimizing data duplication. Row filtering applies during both the initial load and subsequent incremental updates, and is supported for SaaS connectors including Google Analytics, Salesforce, and ServiceNow, as well as all query-based connectors.

See Select rows to ingest.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Ontology snippets (Public Preview): Genie One now supports ontology snippets. This feature is in Public Preview. Contact your Databricks account team to sign up. See Genie Ontology.
  • Document edit timestamps: Documents now show the date and time they were last edited. See Documents in Genie One.
  • Links in documents: Documents now support links. See Documents in Genie One.
  • Scheduled tasks: Fixed a bug that prevented scheduled tasks from running. See Scheduled tasks.

articles.title: Genie Agent (formerly Genie Space) enhancements
articles.summary:
• Agent mode is generally available: Agent mode in Genie Agents (formerly Genie Spaces) is now generally available. Agent mode uses multi-step reasoning to answer complex, exploratory questions with a report that includes citations, visualizations, and supporting tables. See Genie Agents concepts.
  • Retrieve visualization results using the API (Beta): You can now retrieve visualization results from Genie Agents (formerly Genie Spaces) using the API. See the Conversation API reference and the Genie API reference.
  • Upload local files for analysis: You can now upload local Excel and CSV files to an Agent Mode chat for ad-hoc analysis. See Upload a file to a Genie Agent.
  • Expanded chat history: Fixed a bug where each user's chat history was limited to 20 past conversations. Chat history is no longer capped. See Review chats.
  • Add to Dashboard permission fix: Fixed a bug where users with Consumer access could see the Add to Dashboard button without permission.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Import reports from Power BI and Tableau: Authors can now import Power BI and Tableau reports as a new AI/BI dashboard directly from the dashboard list page. See Import BI files using Genie Code.
  • Improved metric view reuse when importing: When importing Tableau and Power BI reports as AI/BI dashboards, Genie Code is now more likely to reference existing Unity Catalog metric views instead of creating new ones. See Import BI files using Genie Code.
  • STRING_AGG function: You can now use STRING_AGG to concatenate non-null string values within a group, with an optional custom delimiter. See string_agg aggregate function.
  • Custom Vega visualization improvements: Two enhancements for custom Vega-Lite visualizations. See Custom visualizations in AI/BI dashboards.
    • Cross-filtering now works for Vega-Lite charts. The selection appears in the active filter bar and is preserved in dashboard URLs and share links.
    • Custom Vega-Lite charts can now inherit the dashboard's light or dark mode and custom theme, and authors can reference theme values directly in Vega-Lite expressions.
  • Counter widget comparison styling: Counter widgets now support text styling on the comparison date and conditional coloring on the comparison field. See Counter visualization.
  • More compact filter widgets: Filter widgets on the dashboard canvas now appear more compact.
  • Dynamic table column widths: Table columns now adjust their width automatically based on cell content.
  • Apply filters fix: Fixed a bug where applying filters did not work.
  • Table column resize fix: Fixed an issue where resizing a table column could unintentionally trigger a sort on that column.
  • Combo chart hover fix: Fixed a console error that sometimes occurred when hovering over empty areas of a combo chart.

articles.title: Veeva Vault connector (Beta)
articles.summary:
The Veeva Vault connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

The connector uses Veeva's Direct Data API to ingest all standard objects, custom objects, system tables, and audit trail tables from your Vault instance into Databricks. Authentication uses OAuth 2.0 M2M via Microsoft Entra ID.

See Veeva Vault connector.

articles.title: MySQL integrated CDC pipeline is now in Beta
articles.summary: The integrated CDC pipeline for MySQL is now in Beta. An integrated CDC pipeline ingests change data from MySQL into Databricks using a single pipeline, combining extraction and application into one pipeline update. Unlike the standard gateway-based architecture, an integrated CDC pipeline requires no separate ingestion gateway. See Create an integrated CDC pipeline for MySQL.

articles.title: Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Gemini 3 Pro Image now available as Databricks-hosted models
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Gemini 3 Pro Image as Databricks-hosted models. You can access these models using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Dashboard relationships (Public Preview)
articles.summary: • Dashboard relationships (Public Preview): Build complex multi-fact data models scoped to an AI/BI dashboard. See Dashboard relationships.

articles.title: MATCH_RECOGNIZE is now in Beta
articles.summary: Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime now support the SQL:2016 MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause for row pattern recognition. Enable the Match Recognize preview in workspace preview settings. See MATCH_RECOGNIZE clause.

articles.title: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 now available as a Databricks-hosted model
articles.summary:
Model Serving now supports Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5 as a Databricks-hosted model. Designed for coding, agentic workflows, and professional work at scale, Claude Sonnet 5 delivers near-Opus-level intelligence with Sonnet's cost efficiency and speed. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs.

Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.

articles.title: Run a subset of job tasks with their dependencies
articles.summary: When you run a subset of a job's tasks, you can now expand your selection to include each task's dependencies. Add the + modifier to a task key to also run its upstream tasks (+my_task), its downstream tasks (my_task+), or both (+my_task+). Start a partial run from the UI, the REST API, the Databricks CLI, the SDKs, or Declarative Automation Bundles. See Run a subset of tasks and their dependencies.

articles.title: Lakehouse Real-Time (Beta)
articles.summary: Lakehouse Real-Time (Lakehouse//RT) is now in Beta. Lakehouse//RT is a serverless SQL warehouse type built for low-latency, high-concurrency workloads, delivering sub-second SQL read queries against Unity Catalog tables. Use it to serve analytical data to applications, run operational analytics, and power dashboards for hundreds to thousands of concurrent users. See Lakehouse Real-Time.

articles.title: Lakebase now available in AWS Tokyo region (ap-northeast-1)
articles.summary: Lakebase is now available in ap-northeast-1 (Asia Pacific - Tokyo). For all supported regions, see Region availability. To get started, see Get a Postgres database.

articles.title: Databricks SQL version 2026.20 is now available in Preview
articles.summary:
Databricks SQL version 2026.20 is now available in the Preview channel. Review the following section to learn about new features, behavioral changes, and bug fixes.

New IP address functions

A set of SQL functions is now available for working with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and CIDR blocks, including ip_host, ip_cidr, ip_version, ip_prefix_length, ip_network, ip_network_last, ip_cidr_contains, ip_as_binary, and ip_as_string, along with try_* variants for null-safe behavior. See ip_host function.

NEAREST BY join type

NEAREST BY is now a supported SQL join type for top-K nearest-neighbor queries. See NEAREST BY clause.

DESCRIBE TABLE PARTITION support for v2 catalog tables

DESCRIBE TABLE ... PARTITION is now supported for v2 catalog tables. Previously, this syntax was available only for v1 tables. See DESCRIBE TABLE.

QUALIFY clause

SQL queries now support a QUALIFY clause, which lets you filter on window function results directly in the query. Previously, this required wrapping the query in a subquery. See Window functions.

DESCRIBE EXTENDED AS JSON includes predictive optimization results

DESCRIBE EXTENDED AS JSON now includes predictive optimization evaluation results in its output. Previously, this information wasn't returned in the JSON output. See DESCRIBE TABLE.

MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION fixes

MERGE WITH SCHEMA EVOLUTION now works correctly when the statement includes WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE or references nested columns by alias. Previously, these combinations could fail or silently produce incorrect results.

Metric view window measures respect filters

Window measures in metric views now return correct results when queries use GROUP BY, IN or BETWEEN filters, or mixed predicates on the window's order column. Previously, these filter patterns could produce incorrect results.

Foreign catalog table permissions preserved on refresh

Unity Catalog now preserves table-level permissions on foreign catalog tables, such as Snowflake connection tables, when it refreshes foreign table metadata. Previously, permissions could be removed during a metadata refresh, causing queries to fail with INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS errors.

Fix for LEFT OUTER JOIN LATERAL with EXPLODE

A bug that produced incorrect null values in LEFT OUTER JOIN LATERAL expressions containing EXPLODE is now fixed. Queries that use this construct now return correct results.

Fix for aggregate queries with partial or final aggregation

A bug that caused aggregate queries using partial merge or final aggregation execution to fail because of missing required input attributes is now fixed. Affected queries now run correctly.

Deferred duplicate field ID errors in Parquet

Photon now defers duplicate field_id errors in Parquet schema resolution until the affected field is accessed. Queries that don't reference the duplicate field now succeed instead of failing during schema resolution.

Improved filter estimation in the query optimizer

The query optimizer now more accurately estimates how much data a filter removes. Previously, inaccurate estimates could cause Databricks to load large tables fully into memory during joins, leading to out-of-memory errors.

Faster queries with multiple COUNT(DISTINCT) expressions

Queries with multiple COUNT(DISTINCT) expressions run faster because Databricks now reduces the data earlier in the execution plan instead of expanding it first.

articles.title: SQL alert task in Lakeflow Jobs is now generally available
articles.summary: The SQL alert task in Lakeflow Jobs is now generally available. Use the task to evaluate a Databricks SQL alert as part of a Lakeflow Job. The task returns its evaluation state as a task output value, so downstream tasks can branch on the result. See SQL alert task for jobs.

articles.title: Databricks Runtime maintenance updates (06/29)
articles.summary:
New maintenance updates are available for supported Databricks Runtime versions. These updates include bug fixes, security patches, and performance improvements. For details, see:

  • Databricks Runtime 18
  • Databricks Runtime 18.2
  • Databricks Runtime 18.1
  • Databricks Runtime 18.0
  • Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS
  • Databricks Runtime 16.4 LTS
  • Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS
  • Databricks Runtime 14.3 LTS
  • Databricks Runtime 13.3 LTS

articles.title: Govern LLMs in Unity Catalog with model services (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now govern Databricks-hosted LLMs in Unity Catalog using model services, currently in Beta. A model service is a Unity Catalog securable that represents a governed LLM endpoint, so you can define an endpoint once and share it across workspaces using Unity Catalog privileges, instead of duplicating endpoints per workspace. Databricks provides ready-to-use model services in the system.ai schema for Databricks-hosted foundation models, and you can create your own with the Unity Gateway UI, Catalog Explorer, or the Unity Catalog REST API. See model services.

articles.title: Custom Docker images for AI Runtime CLI workloads (Beta)
articles.summary: You can now bring your own Docker container image to AI Runtime CLI (air) workloads. This feature is in Beta. Use a custom image when you need specific system library versions, complex dependencies, or a reproducible environment. See Use custom Docker images with the legacy Python CLI.

articles.title: Parquet v2 for Delta Lake tables is generally available
articles.summary: Parquet v2 is now generally available for Delta Lake tables in Databricks Runtime 18.1 and above. Parquet v2 uses advanced encodings, v2 data page headers, and INT64 timestamps to improve query performance and reduce table sizes. To use, set the delta.parquet.format.version table property to 2.12.0 or enable automatic upgrades. See Parquet v2 and Automatic upgrades.

articles.title: Genie Code Chat/Agent mode selector removed
articles.summary:
The Chat/Agent mode selector has been removed from the Genie Code pane. Genie Code now runs exclusively in Agent mode. If you prefer a conversational response without autonomous task execution (what was previously called Chat mode), include that instruction in your prompt. For example: "Just explain this to me, don't run any code."

See Genie Code.

articles.title: ai_parse_document quality improvements: checkboxes, forms, and complex tables
articles.summary: ai_parse_document improves extraction from checkboxes, forms, and complex tables. See ai_parse_document function.

articles.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365 connector (GA)
articles.summary: The managed Microsoft Dynamics 365 connector in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available. The connector allows you to ingest CRM and ERP data from Dynamics 365 into Databricks using Azure Synapse Link. See Microsoft Dynamics 365 connector.

articles.title: Metric view parameters are now in Public Preview
articles.summary: You can now define parameters in metric views to bind values at query time, serving many query variants from a single definition instead of maintaining a separate metric view per variant. See Use parameters with metric views.

articles.title: Customer-managed VPC will soon be required for classic workspaces
articles.summary:
In a future release, Databricks plans to deprecate classic workspace creation with a Databricks-managed VPC. New classic workspaces will require a customer-managed VPC. For the simplest quick start, use a serverless workspace. A detailed migration timeline will be communicated separately.

See Configure a customer-managed VPC.

articles.title: Databricks Runtime 19 (Beta): June 26, 2026
articles.summary:
Behavioral changes

  • Environment variable availability restricted in standard access mode: In standard access mode, only a predefined set of environment variables is available to the Spark engine and init scripts. This set includes common configuration variables, such as proxy settings (HTTP_PROXY), cloud credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID), and catalog variables (CATALOG). Other variables that you set on a cluster remain available to your user code, including UDFs, but are not available to the Spark engine or init scripts. Previously, all cluster environment variables were available to the Spark engine and init scripts. See Environment variable limitations.
  • Restricted Spark configurations in standard access mode: In standard access mode, you can no longer set certain Spark configuration properties. Creating or editing a cluster that sets a restricted property (matched by prefix) fails with an error. Restricted properties include spark.driver.extraJavaOptions, spark.executor.extraJavaOptions, spark.jars, spark.files, spark.executorEnv.*, and spark.kubernetes.*, among others. Previously, you could set these properties in standard access mode. Remove them from your cluster configuration before upgrading. For the complete list, see Spark configuration limitations.

articles.title: Solution Accelerators in Databricks Marketplace are now published as apps or notebooks
articles.summary: Solution Accelerators are no longer a separate listing type in Databricks Marketplace. The content is unchanged, but they are now categorized as apps (interactive applications) or notebooks (code-based accelerators). See What is Databricks Marketplace?.

articles.title: Genie One enhancements
articles.summary:
• Share chats with account users: You can now share Genie One chats with all users in your account as read-only. See Share a chat.
  • New external source connections (Beta): Chat in Genie One now supports connecting to Gmail and additional Microsoft 365 apps (Teams, Outlook, and Calendar). See Connect Genie One to external tools and sources.
  • Scheduled task frequency limit: Scheduled tasks can no longer be created with a frequency greater than daily. Hourly and per-minute frequencies are no longer supported. Contact your Databricks account team if you require more frequent scheduling.
  • Scheduled task email prefix: Scheduled task notification emails now use the prefix "Genie Task:" instead of "Task update:".

articles.title: Genie Agent (formerly Genie Space) enhancements
articles.summary: • Genie Code space authoring skills: Genie Code now includes dedicated skills for authoring and maintaining Genie Agents (formerly Genie Spaces). See Create a Genie Agent and Debug responses with Genie Code.

articles.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
articles.summary:
• Dynamic annotation lines: Annotation lines can now be driven by data or a calculation instead of a fixed value, letting you show running averages, variable thresholds, or anomaly markers that update with your data. See Annotations.
  • Six new preset themes: Six new built-in color and style themes are now available for AI/BI dashboards, giving authors more ready-made options without creating a custom theme. See Choose a preset theme.
  • Local metric view and dashboard relationship fix: Fixed a bug where local metric views and dashboard relationships sometimes failed when referencing assets from a Hive Metastore.
  • Faceted chart fix: Fixed an issue where faceted charts with a DECIMAL facet column dropped most rows in each facet.
  • Combo chart hover bug fix: Fixed an issue where hovering over buckets with null line or area values showed an incorrect tooltip and drew a stray point at the baseline. Null values now remain null instead of displaying as 0.

articles.title: Databricks connector for Power Platform is generally available
articles.summary: The Databricks connector for Microsoft Power Platform is now generally available. See Databricks and Microsoft Power Platform integration.

articles.title: Change the owner of standalone pipeline streaming tables and materialized views
articles.summary: You can now use ALTER STREAMING TABLE and ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW with SET OWNER TO to change the owner of streaming tables and materialized views backed by standalone pipelines created in Databricks SQL. See Use ALTER statements with pipeline datasets.

articles.title: Standalone pipeline materialized views support expectations
articles.summary: You can now add data quality expectations to materialized views created in Databricks SQL using the CONSTRAINT expectation_name EXPECT (expectation_expr) clause. Expectations let you validate records as they flow through the standalone pipeline that backs the materialized view, and warn, drop, or fail on records that violate a constraint. Streaming tables created in Databricks SQL already support expectations. See Manage data quality with pipeline expectations.
